accordion.name: Accordion
accordion.definition:
A set of expand/collapse sections built on Disclosure, stacked into
one divider-separated list. Each section holds its state on its native
`<details>` element; giving sibling Accordion.Items the same `name`
makes the set exclusive through the platform's `<details name>` behavior,
closing whichever section was open as another opens.
accordion.summary: A set of expand/collapse sections built on Disclosure, stacked into one divider-separated list.
accordion.description:
Renders the list's root host: a plain `<div>` that stacks
Accordion.Item sections in normal block flow, each drawing its own
divider so the whole list reads as one continuous group.
examples:
{t("faq.refunds.question")}

{t("faq.refunds.answer")}

 {t("faq.shipping.question")}

{t("faq.shipping.answer")}

rows.name: children
rows.description: One or more Accordion.Item sections to stack into a list.

parts.name: Accordion.Item
parts.description: Renders one section as Disclosure restyled into a flush list row: only a shared block-end divider survives, restored block-start on the first section.

parts.name: Accordion.Trigger
parts.description: Renders Accordion.TriggerProps.children as the section's label row, spread to opposite ends and underlined on hover.

parts.name: Accordion.Content
parts.description: Renders Accordion.ContentProps.children as the section's revealed body: Disclosure.Panel restyled with block-end padding and small, muted text sized for supporting copy.

alert-dialog.name: AlertDialog
alert-dialog.definition:
An interruptive modal surface that demands an explicit response before a
page continues — confirming a destructive action, surfacing a blocking
error — built on the native `<dialog>` host of Dialog, widened for
its two-button layout and sealed against light dismiss. Its compound parts
cover a header, title, description, and a two-control footer.
alert-dialog.summary: An interruptive modal surface that demands an explicit response before a page continues — confirming a destructive action, surfacing a blocking error — built on the native `<dialog>` host of Dialog, widened for its two-button layout and sealed against light dismiss.
alert-dialog.description:
Renders the alert panel through Dialog, widened to fit a two-button
footer, with `role` fixed to `"alertdialog"` and `closedby` to
`"closerequest"` so the interruption clears through an explicit response.

parts.name: AlertDialog.Header
parts.description: Renders AlertDialog.HeaderProps.children as the panel's header slot: a column stacking AlertDialog.Title and AlertDialog.Description with a small gap between them.

parts.name: AlertDialog.Title
parts.description: Renders AlertDialog.TitleProps.children as the panel's heading, inside the native heading element matching the nearest ancestor `HeadingScope`'s depth, or `<h1>` where no scope wraps it.

parts.name: AlertDialog.Description
parts.description:
Renders AlertDialog.DescriptionProps.children as the panel's supporting copy, in a native `

` set to the panel's muted foreground color so it reads as secondary to AlertDialog.Title.

parts.name: AlertDialog.Footer
parts.description: Renders AlertDialog.FooterProps.children as an end-aligned action row.

parts.name: AlertDialog.Action
parts.description: Renders the panel's emphasized action as a danger-toned Button, typed `"button"` so its `command="close"` reaches the AlertDialog named by `commandfor`; `type="submit"` submits the enclosing form instead.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of the ancestor AlertDialog this action dismisses. Required for the default `type="button"` action; a `type="submit"` action ends the interruption by submitting its enclosing form.

rows.name: command
rows.description: Invoker Commands verb dispatched to the target AlertDialog. Defaults to `"close"`, and is dropped for a `"submit"` or `"reset"` action, which the platform drives as a form control instead of an invoker.

parts.name: AlertDialog.Cancel
parts.description: Renders the panel's dismiss control as an outline, neutral Button with `type` fixed to `"button"`, so its `command="close"` reaches the AlertDialog named by `commandfor` from inside a `<form>` too.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of the ancestor AlertDialog this cancel control dismisses.

rows.name: command
rows.description: Invoker Commands verb dispatched to the target AlertDialog. Defaults to `"close"`.

rows.name: type
rows.description: Narrowed to the only value a cancel control carries, and always rendered, since the platform runs its close command only from a button typed `"button"`, including inside a `<form>`.

alert.name: Alert
alert.definition:
An inline status message rendered as a bordered, tinted panel, colored by
one of five semantic tones and announced to assistive technology through
`role="alert"` plus a configurable `aria-live` politeness. Compound parts
cover an optional leading icon, a title/description content block, and a
trailing action, so a page composes only the parts a given message needs.
alert.summary: An inline status message rendered as a bordered, tinted panel, colored by one of five semantic tones and announced to assistive technology through `role="alert"` plus a configurable `aria-live` politeness.
alert.description:
Renders an inline status panel tinted by Alert.Props.color, gaining
inline-start padding through `:has()` when a direct Alert.Icon
needs the room. `role`, `aria-atomic`, and `aria-live` stay overridable.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic tone of the alert. Default: `"neutral"`.

rows.name: live
rows.description: `aria-live` politeness for dynamic alerts. Default: `"polite"`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The alert's compound parts: Alert.Icon, Alert.Content, Alert.Action, or any other content.

parts.name: Alert.Icon
parts.description: Renders Alert.IconProps.children as the alert's leading icon, absolutely positioned at the panel's inline/block-start corner with any direct SVG sized to `1rem`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The icon graphic, typically a single SVG icon.

parts.name: Alert.Content
parts.description: Renders Alert.ContentProps.children as the alert's body block: a column flex container that shrinks to fit alongside a leading icon or trailing action, holding Alert.Title and Alert.Description.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The alert's title, description, or other body content.

parts.name: Alert.Title
parts.description: Renders Alert.TitleProps.children as the alert's heading, inside the native heading element matching the nearest ancestor `HeadingScope`'s depth — or `<h1>` where no scope wraps it — styled as a small, tight label.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The alert's heading text.

parts.name: Alert.Description
parts.description: Renders Alert.DescriptionProps.children as the alert's supporting message, slightly translucent against the alert's foreground color so it reads as secondary to the title.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The alert's supporting message text.

parts.name: Alert.Action
parts.description: Renders Alert.ActionProps.children as the alert's trailing control — a button, link, or dismiss affordance — pinned to the panel's block-start edge at its own natural size.

rows.name: children
rows.description: A button, link, or other control the alert offers, e.g. "Retry" or "Dismiss".

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic tone driving the host element's border, tint, and foreground color through the `--ui-*` variables for that color.

types.name: Live
types.description: `aria-live` politeness applied to the host element.

aspect-ratio.name: AspectRatio
aspect-ratio.definition:
A layout primitive that locks its host to a fixed width-to-height ratio,
clipping whatever content it wraps so the box keeps its shape regardless
of the content's own intrinsic size. It reserves stable space for media,
embeds, and other loading content ahead of time, so nothing around it
shifts once that content resolves its own measurements.
aspect-ratio.summary: A layout primitive that locks its host to a fixed width-to-height ratio, clipping whatever content it wraps so the box keeps its shape regardless of the content's own intrinsic size.
aspect-ratio.description:
Fills its container's inline axis and clips any overflow. The ratio rides on
the `--ui-aspect-ratio` custom property, set per instance from the `ratio`
prop, so an ancestor's stylesheet can override it on its own.

rows.name: ratio
rows.description: Width-to-height ratio the host maintains. Defaults to a square.

attachment.name: Attachment
attachment.definition:
A compound card presenting one attached file or image — media preview, name,
supporting details, actions — plus a horizontally scrolling row for several
cards side by side. Every part styles itself off the card's own `state`, and
whole-card click-through stays an opt-in wrapper a consumer mixes in.
attachment.summary: A compound card presenting one attached file or image — media preview, name, supporting details, actions — plus a horizontally scrolling row for several cards side by side.
attachment.description:
The card's outer host, recolored to the danger tint at `state="error"` and
declaring the `ui-attachment` named container so nested parts reflow at the
card's width. A busy state sets `aria-busy` to the token ARIA recognizes.

rows.name: state
rows.description: Lifecycle state of the file or image the card represents. Defaults to `"idle"`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The card's compound parts: Attachment.Media, Attachment.Content, and Attachment.Actions.

parts.name: Attachment.Media
parts.description: The card's media well: a fixed-size, rounded box clipping the preview a consumer nests inside.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The preview itself: an ``, or a decorative icon standing in for the file's type.

parts.name: Attachment.Content
parts.description: The card's text column, growing into whatever inline space Attachment.Media and Attachment.Actions leave it.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Attachment.Title and, optionally, Attachment.Description.

parts.name: Attachment.Title
parts.description:
The file or image name in a native `

`, truncated to a single line with an ellipsis.

rows.name: state
rows.description: The ancestor Attachment's own `state`, repeated here because a component reads only its own props; passing the same value to both is what keeps them in sync. Left unset, the title renders plain.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The file or image name.

parts.name: Attachment.Description
parts.description:
The card's supporting detail line: a muted, single-line `

` carrying a file size, a page count, or the explanation of what went wrong once the ancestor Attachment's `state` reads `"error"`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Supporting detail — a file size, a page count, an error message.

parts.name: Attachment.Actions
parts.description: The card's action row, shrink-proof so a narrow card's width is absorbed by Attachment.Content's own truncation while the actions keep their size.

rows.name: children
rows.description: A run of Attachment.Action controls.

parts.name: Attachment.Action
parts.description: A single card action as a Button, defaulting to a compact, `"ghost"`, neutral control so a row of actions reads as secondary to the card's title.

parts.name: Attachment.Trigger
parts.description: A wrapper `<div>` whose `href` or `commandfor` stays an inert attribute until a consumer mixes in `attachmentTrigger()`.

rows.name: href
rows.description: Destination the whole card follows once `attachmentTrigger()` is mixed in, opened in place unless the activation asks for a new tab. It rides on a `<div>` so a nested Attachment.Action stays valid markup.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of a `<dialog>` element the whole card opens once `attachmentTrigger()` is mixed in, instead of following `href`.

rows.name: command
rows.description: Invoker Commands verb dispatched to `commandfor`'s dialog. Defaults to `"show-modal"`.

rows.name: target
rows.description: Where `href` opens: a window/frame name, or `"_blank"` for a new tab. Meaningful only alongside `href`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The card's own markup — typically an Attachment.

parts.name: Attachment.Group
parts.description: A horizontally scroll-snapping row of cards, faded at both inline edges to hint at cards beyond the current view.

rows.name: children
rows.description: A run of Attachment or Attachment.Trigger cards.

types.name: State
types.description: Lifecycle state of a card's file or image.

avatar.name: Avatar
avatar.definition:
A person's or entity's picture rendered as a fixed-size, fully circular
host stacking an image layer, an initials fallback, and an optional corner
status badge, plus a way to overlap several instances into one group with
a trailing overflow count. The circular shape stays fixed, since a profile
picture always renders fully rounded.
avatar.summary: A person's or entity's picture rendered as a fixed-size, fully circular host stacking an image layer, an initials fallback, and an optional corner status badge, plus a way to overlap several instances into one group with a trailing overflow count.
avatar.description:
Renders a fixed-size, fully circular picture host sized through the
`data-size` attribute contract (`"sm"`, `"md"`, or `"lg"`), stacking
whichever image, fallback, and badge parts a consumer composes as children.

badge.name: Badge
badge.definition:
A compact pill communicating a short status, label, or count inline with
surrounding content. Its host renders solid, tinted, or outlined depending
on a variant attribute, colored through a semantic color role, and
composes with `Icon` and `Text` parts for glyph-plus-label badges.
badge.summary: A compact pill communicating a short status, label, or count inline with surrounding content.
badge.description:
Renders a single-line pill host, colored and shaped through the
`data-color` and `data-variant` attribute contract: `"default"` fills the
pill solid, `"secondary"` tints the fill, `"outline"` keeps just a border.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: variant
rows.description: Visual weight. Defaults to DEFAULT_VARIANT.

parts.name: Badge.Icon
parts.description: Renders the badge's leading or trailing glyph slot: an inert, shrink-proof `<span>` sized to hold a single small icon and hidden from assistive technology, since Badge.Text carries the badge's meaning.

parts.name: Badge.Text
parts.description: Renders the badge's label slot: a `<span>` with its line height collapsed to one, keeping short label text vertically centered inside the pill.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

types.name: Variant
types.description: Visual weight the badge renders with: a solid fill, a tinted fill, or a transparent chip with just an outline.

breadcrumbs.name: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.definition:
A trail of links marking the page's position within a hierarchy of parent
sections, composing a `<nav>` root, an `<ol>` list, and `<li>` items around
Breadcrumbs.Link, a restyled Link. Every item but the last
draws its separator through a CSS `::after` pseudo-element, keeping it
purely presentational, and the trail's current segment reads straight from
the native `aria-current` attribute a consumer sets while rendering the
page it currently occupies.
breadcrumbs.summary: A trail of links marking the page's position within a hierarchy of parent sections, composing a `<nav>` root, an `<ol>` list, and `<li>` items around Breadcrumbs.Link, a restyled Link.
breadcrumbs.description:
Renders the trail's `<nav>` root, laying Breadcrumbs.List as a row.
A root missing `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` logs a dev-mode
`console.warn`, since assistive technology needs one to identify this landmark.

parts.name: Breadcrumbs.List
parts.description: Renders the trail's `<ol>` list, resetting native list markers and spacing and laying Breadcrumbs.Item children out as a wrapped row with a small gap between them.

parts.name: Breadcrumbs.Item
parts.description: Renders a single `<li>` wrapping one Breadcrumbs.Link.

parts.name: Breadcrumbs.Link
parts.description: Renders one trail segment as a restyled Link: sized to `0.875rem` with its underline dropped, defaulting to a quiet neutral color role that brightens on hover and bolds when `aria-current="page"` is set.

bubble.name: Bubble
bubble.definition:
The framed message surface inside a conversational row's content slot,
sized to its own content up to a share of the row's width. Variants cover
tones from a solid fill to fully unframed, and `align` hugs either row
edge. `Bubble.Content`, `Bubble.Reactions`, and `Bubble.Group` compose the
turn's text, its reaction toggles, and multi-bubble runs.
bubble.summary: The framed message surface inside a conversational row's content slot, sized to its own content up to a share of the row's width.
bubble.description:
Renders the frame, pushed to the edge `align` names via auto margins so it
aligns correctly regardless of its row's layout. Its nearest corner falls
back to a literal `0.125rem`, since `roundedCorner()` has no `"xs"` step.

rows.name: variant
rows.description: Visual weight. Defaults to DEFAULT_VARIANT.

rows.name: align
rows.description: Edge of the row the frame hugs. Defaults to DEFAULT_ALIGN.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The frame's compound parts: Bubble.Content, an optional Bubble.Reactions, or any other content.

parts.name: Bubble.Content
parts.description: Renders Bubble.ContentProps.children as the frame's padded text slot, breaking long unbroken runs at the inline box edge and taking its text color from the ancestor Bubble's `variant` via CSS inheritance.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The turn's text — plain, or wrapped in a typography layer for rendered markdown.

parts.name: Bubble.Reactions
parts.description: Renders Bubble.ReactionsProps.children as a `role="group"` row: a negative block-start margin pins it into the frame's lower padding, aligned via the `--ui-bubble-reactions-justify` property the frame sets from `align`.

rows.name: "aria-label"
rows.description: Accessible label describing the row as a set of reactions.

rows.name: children
rows.description: One or more already-pressed toggle controls, each scoped to a single reaction.

parts.name: Bubble.Group
parts.description: Renders Bubble.GroupProps.children as a tightly spaced column of consecutive Bubble frames, softening only the corners touching a neighbor to a smaller radius, so the run reads as one continuous shape.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Two or more Bubble frames from the same turn, stacked into one run.

types.name: Variant
types.description: Visual weight the frame renders with: solid `"default"`/`"secondary"` fills, soft `"muted"`/`"tinted"` tints, a bordered `"outline"`, an unframed `"ghost"`, and a solid danger fill for `"destructive"`.

types.name: Align
types.description: Edge of the row the frame hugs: `"start"` stays flush with the row's leading edge (flipping under `dir="rtl"`), `"end"` stays flush with the trailing edge, typically paired with the reader's own turns vs everyone else's.

button.name: Button
button.definition:
An interactive control for a single, immediate action — submitting a form,
triggering a command, opening a dialog. Its host renders as a native
`<button>` shaped by a semantic color role, a visual weight variant, and a
size, and holds its footprint while rendering a busy pending state.
button.summary: An interactive control for a single, immediate action — submitting a form, triggering a command, opening a dialog.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: variant
rows.description: Visual weight. Defaults to DEFAULT_VARIANT.

rows.name: size
rows.description: Size variant. Defaults to DEFAULT_SIZE.

rows.name: isPending
rows.description: Marks the button busy: merges into the native `disabled` attribute and swaps the visible content for a spinner glyph while holding the rendered footprint, so a page mid-request keeps its layout.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the pending state's internal elements.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

types.name: Variant
types.description: Visual weight the button renders with: a solid fill with an on-solid foreground, a transparent fill with a strong colored border, or a fully transparent fill with just a colored label.

types.name: Size
types.description: Size variant controlling the button's padding and font size.

calendar.name: Calendar
calendar.definition:
A month-grid calendar surface composed from a navigable header and a native
`<table>` of day cells, styled through the platform's own semantics. Used
bare, it renders a native `<input type="date">` — a complete,
keyboard-operable date control on its own.
calendar.summary: A month-grid calendar surface composed from a navigable header and a native `<table>` of day cells, styled through the platform's own semantics.
calendar.description:
Renders a rounded, padded surface around whichever children a consumer
composes; `children` left unset renders a native `<input type="date">`
through Input, the one part the platform itself operates.
examples:
<Calendar aria-label={t("calendar.label")}>
	<Calendar.Header>
		<Calendar.PreviousButton aria-label={t("calendar.previous")} />
		<Calendar.Heading>{monthLabel}</Calendar.Heading>
		<Calendar.NextButton aria-label={t("calendar.next")} />
	</Calendar.Header>
	<Calendar.Grid aria-label={monthLabel}>
		<Calendar.GridHeader>
			<Calendar.Row>
				{weekdayLabels.map((day) => (
					<Calendar.HeaderCell key={day}>{day}</Calendar.HeaderCell>
				))}
			</Calendar.Row>
		</Calendar.GridHeader>
		<Calendar.GridBody>
			{weeks.map((week) => (
				<Calendar.Row key={week[0].iso}>
					{week.map((day) => (
						<Calendar.Cell
							key={day.iso}
							aria-selected={day.iso === selected ? "true" : undefined}
							data-outside-month={day.outsideMonth ? "" : undefined}
						>
							{day.label}
						</Calendar.Cell>
					))}
				</Calendar.Row>
			))}
		</Calendar.GridBody>
	</Calendar.Grid>
</Calendar>

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the bare fallback control's focus ring. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form, read only by the bare fallback control.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a bare fallback control a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Initial value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a bare fallback control left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: min
rows.description: Earliest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read only by the bare fallback control.

rows.name: max
rows.description: Latest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read only by the bare fallback control.

rows.name: step
rows.description: Granularity, in days, the bare fallback control's value must fall on.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the bare fallback control required for its enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the bare fallback control inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks the bare fallback control's value fixed, while keeping it focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint for the bare fallback control, e.g. `"bday"`.

parts.name: Calendar.Header
parts.description: Renders Calendar's nav row: a flex row spacing Calendar.PreviousButton, Calendar.Heading, and Calendar.NextButton apart, the heading centered between the controls.

parts.name: Calendar.PreviousButton
parts.description: Renders a round icon control standing for "show the previous month", sized to match Calendar.NextButton.

parts.name: Calendar.NextButton
parts.description: Renders a round icon control standing for "show the following month", with the rendering, focus, and disabled-state contract of Calendar.PreviousButton and a trailing chevron by default.

parts.name: Calendar.Heading
parts.description: Renders the consumer-formatted month/year caption through Heading, centered between the nav controls at a small semibold size layered after Heading's own defaults, so this size and alignment win over them.

parts.name: Calendar.Grid
parts.description: Renders the day grid's native `<table>` host, rows and cells set apart by a small gap on every side.

parts.name: Calendar.GridHeader
parts.description: Renders the grid's `<thead>` host: a plain wrapper for the weekday Calendar.Row.

parts.name: Calendar.Row
parts.description: Renders a native `<tr>` host: one row of Calendar.HeaderCell inside Calendar.GridHeader, or one week of Calendar.Cell inside Calendar.GridBody.

parts.name: Calendar.HeaderCell
parts.description: Renders a weekday abbreviation inside a native `<th scope="col">`, sized small and muted beneath Calendar.Cell's own larger day numbers.

parts.name: Calendar.GridBody
parts.description: Renders the grid's `<tbody>` host: a plain wrapper for one Calendar.Row per week.

parts.name: Calendar.Cell
parts.description: Renders one calendar day inside a native `<td>`, a fixed round pill around its number.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role for the bare `<input type="date">` fallback's keyboard focus ring, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

card.name: Card
card.definition:
A bounded container grouping a header, body content, and footer actions
into one bordered, softly shadowed panel tinted by a semantic color role.
The role colors border, background, and text together, so Card.Title
and Card.Description inherit their text color from the root through
ordinary CSS inheritance.
card.summary: A bounded container grouping a header, body content, and footer actions into one bordered, softly shadowed panel tinted by a semantic color role.
card.description:
The card panel: a rounded, bordered, softly shadowed `<section>` tinted
through the `data-color` attribute contract. Compose Card.Header,
Card.Content, and Card.Footer inside it.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

parts.name: Card.Header
parts.description: Renders the card's header slot: a `<header>` stacking its children in a column with a small gap, padded on every side.

parts.name: Card.Title
parts.description: The card's heading, in the native heading element matching the nearest ambient heading level — `<h1>` where nothing supplies one.

parts.name: Card.Description
parts.description:
Renders the card's supporting copy inside a native `

`, muted to seventy percent opacity so it reads as secondary to Card.Title.

parts.name: Card.Content
parts.description: The card's main body slot: a `<div>` padded on its inline and block-end edges, leaving its block-start edge flush against Card.Header.

parts.name: Card.Footer
parts.description: The card's footer slot: a `<footer>` laying its children out in a vertically centered row, padded on its inline and block-end edges so it sits flush against the content above.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` border, background, and foreground variables.

carousel.name: Carousel
carousel.definition:
A horizontally scrolling collection of slides riding native CSS scroll snap,
so swiping or scrolling advances between slides with no script in the
baseline. Carousel.Viewport is the scrolling surface,
Carousel.Track rows up its Carousel.Slide children, and
Carousel.Previous/Carousel.Next are invoker buttons a paired
mixin wires into working controls.
carousel.summary: A horizontally scrolling collection of slides riding native CSS scroll snap, so swiping or scrolling advances between slides with no script in the baseline.
carousel.description:
The carousel root: a `<section>` stacking Carousel.Viewport and
Carousel.Controls in a column, declaring the `--ui-carousel-*`
custom properties its descendants read with per-instance defaults.

parts.name: Carousel.Viewport
parts.description: A `<div>` scrolling Carousel.Track along the inline axis via logical properties for correct writing direction, with mandatory scroll-snap stops; scroll padding reads `--ui-carousel-padding` to clear the track's own padding.

parts.name: Carousel.Track
parts.description: The carousel's slide row: a `<div>` laying its Carousel.Slide children out in one inline row, gapped by `--ui-carousel-gap` and padded by `--ui-carousel-padding` so the first and last slide can still center.

parts.name: Carousel.Slide
parts.description: A single slide: a `<div>` held at `--ui-carousel-slide-size` along the inline axis, with a mandatory snap stop at its inline-start edge so the viewport settles on a slide boundary.

parts.name: Carousel.Controls
parts.description: The carousel's control row: a `<div>` laying Carousel.Previous and Carousel.Next out as an end-aligned, vertically centered row.

parts.name: Carousel.Previous
parts.description: A static control scrolling Carousel.Viewport named by `commandfor` back one slide when a hydrated `carouselControls()` mixin handles `"--ui-prev"`; custom `children` replacing the chevron still need their own `aria-label`.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of the Carousel.Viewport this control scrolls back through.

rows.name: command
rows.description: Invoker Commands verb a `carouselControls()` mixin listens for. Defaults to `"--ui-prev"`.

parts.name: Carousel.Next
parts.description: A static control scrolling Carousel.Viewport named by `commandfor` forward one slide when a hydrated `carouselControls()` mixin handles `"--ui-next"`; custom `children` replacing the chevron still need their own `aria-label`.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of the Carousel.Viewport this control scrolls forward through.

rows.name: command
rows.description: Invoker Commands verb a `carouselControls()` mixin listens for. Defaults to `"--ui-next"`.

chart.name: Chart
chart.definition:
The `Chart` namespace's compound parts, covering Cartesian series
(Chart, Chart.Line, Chart.Area, Chart.Bar)
and the independent Chart.Pie root, each pairing with
Chart.Legend for a script-free series switcher and
Chart.Tooltip for a richer hover surface.
chart.summary: The `Chart` namespace's compound parts, covering Cartesian series (Chart, Chart.Line, Chart.Area, Chart.Bar) and the independent Chart.Pie root, each pairing with Chart.Legend for a script-free series switcher and Chart.Tooltip for a richer hover surface.
chart.description:
Renders a chart's coordinate space: a responsive `<svg>` whose `viewBox`
comes from `width`/`height`, shared via context so nested series share one
scale. A paired Chart.Legend must render as this root's later sibling.
examples:
<Chart width={480} height={240} xDomain={[0, 11]} yDomain={[0, 1000]} aria-label={t("chart.revenue.label")}>
	<Chart.Line
		points={months.map((month) => ({
			x: month.index,
			y: month.revenue,
			label: t("chart.revenue.point", { month: month.name, amount: month.revenue }),
		}))}
	/>
</Chart>
<Chart.Legend aria-label={t("chart.legend")}>
	<Chart.Legend.Item color={1}>{t("chart.series.revenue")}</Chart.Legend.Item>
</Chart.Legend>

rows.name: width
rows.description: Pixel width of the chart's internal coordinate space — the value every nested series' `x` positions are mapped onto. The `<svg>` renders at its container's full size, scaling this space while preserving aspect ratio.

rows.name: height
rows.description: Pixel height of the chart's internal coordinate space — the value every nested series' `y` positions are mapped onto.

rows.name: xDomain
rows.description: `[start, end]` bounds of every nested series' horizontal data values, mapped across `width` and shared through context so every series lines up on the same horizontal scale.

rows.name: yDomain
rows.description: `[start, end]` bounds of every nested series' vertical data values, mapped across `height`. `start` maps to the coordinate space's bottom edge and `end` to its top, matching a value axis growing upward against SVG's `y`.

parts.name: Chart.Line
parts.description: Renders a line series: a stroked, `aria-hidden` `<path>` connecting `points` via linearScale and linePath, plus a focusable marker with a `<title>`, sampled via ticks for manageable density.

rows.name: points
rows.description: The series' data points, in draw order along `x`. The plotted path connects every point given here; the accessible markers render on only a representative spread of them, chosen through `markerCount`.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Categorical color. Defaults to DEFAULT_LINE_COLOR.

rows.name: markerCount
rows.description: Approximate number of accessible, hoverable markers placed along `points`. Each marker snaps to the point closest to one of this many evenly spread "nice" values across the ancestor Chart's `xDomain`.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the plotted `path` and each point `marker`, layered after each part's own built-in styling. Use the `mix` prop instead to style the series' outer host.

parts.name: Chart.Area
parts.description: Renders an area series: a filled, `aria-hidden` `<path>` tracing `points` and closing down to `baseline`, mapped through linearScale and areaPath, plus a focusable marker sampled via ticks.

rows.name: points
rows.description: The series' data points, in draw order along `x`. The filled region traces every point given here before closing down to `baseline`; markers render on a representative spread of them, chosen through `markerCount`.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Categorical color. Defaults to DEFAULT_AREA_COLOR.

rows.name: baseline
rows.description: The `yDomain` value the filled region closes down (or up) to — typically the value axis' zero line. Defaults to DEFAULT_AREA_BASELINE.

rows.name: markerCount
rows.description: Approximate number of accessible, hoverable markers placed along `points`. Each marker snaps to the point closest to one of this many evenly spread "nice" values across the ancestor Chart's `xDomain`.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the filled `path` and each point `marker`, layered after each part's own built-in styling. Use the `mix` prop instead to style the series' outer host.

parts.name: Chart.Pie
parts.description: Renders a pie or donut chart: an independent `<svg>` root, since a circular layout shares no domain with a Cartesian Chart.

rows.name: data
rows.description: The wedges to draw, in draw order. Each entry's position in this list picks its default color when its own `color` is omitted.

rows.name: width
rows.description: Pixel width of the chart's internal coordinate space that `viewBox` maps onto. The rendered `<svg>` fills `100%` of the host's own inline size, scaled to fit while preserving this aspect ratio against `height`.

rows.name: height
rows.description: Pixel height of the chart's internal coordinate space, on the same terms as `width`.

rows.name: innerRadius
rows.description: Pixel distance from center to every wedge's inner edge, in the same coordinate space as `width`/`height`. A positive value smaller than the chart's outer radius produces a donut with a hole that size.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for every wedge `segment`, layered after its own built-in styling. Use the `mix` prop instead to style the chart's outer host.

parts.name: Chart.Bar
parts.description: Renders a categorical bar chart: an independent `<svg>` root, since a band axis shares no continuous domain with a Cartesian Chart.

rows.name: data
rows.description: Rows to plot, one band per row along the category axis, in draw order.

rows.name: series
rows.description: Ordered series keys plotted within every row's band. A key's position in this list is both the stable index stamped onto `data-series-index` and its slot in the `--ui-chart-1`–`--ui-chart-8` palette, wrapping past it.

rows.name: width
rows.description: Pixel width of the chart's internal coordinate space that `viewBox` maps onto. The rendered `<svg>` fills `100%` of the host's own inline size, scaled to fit while preserving this aspect ratio against `height`.

rows.name: height
rows.description: Pixel height of the chart's internal coordinate space, on the same terms as `width`.

rows.name: domain
rows.description: `[start, end]` bounds of every bar's value, mapped across `height`. `start` maps to the bottom edge and `end` to the top, matching the same upward-value convention Chart.Props.yDomain uses against SVG's `y`.

rows.name: tickCount
rows.description: Approximate number of horizontal gridlines spanning `domain`. Defaults to DEFAULT_BAR_TICK_COUNT.

rows.name: categoryGap
rows.description: Fraction of each category band reserved as a gap from its neighbors. Defaults to DEFAULT_CATEGORY_GAP.

rows.name: seriesGap
rows.description: Fraction of each category's own band reserved as a gap between its series' bars — most bar charts plot a single series per category, with no neighboring bar to gap against.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the gridlines and bars, layered after each part's own built-in styling. Use the `mix` prop instead to style the chart's outer host.

checkbox-group.name: CheckboxGroup
checkbox-group.definition:
A landmark grouping independently toggled checkbox controls into one
related set: a `role="group"` host laying children out in a column, or a
row when `orientation` is `"horizontal"`. Each nested checkbox keeps its
own checked state, `name`, and `value`; the host contributes the shared
grouping, the layout, and an invalid-state color for composed text.
checkbox-group.summary: A landmark grouping independently toggled checkbox controls into one related set: a `role="group"` host laying children out in a column, or a row when `orientation` is `"horizontal"`.
checkbox-group.description:
Lays checkbox children out in a column, or a row when `orientation` is
`"horizontal"`; each nested checkbox keeps its own checked state, `name`,
and `value`. `aria-invalid="true"` recolors plain text composed alongside.
examples:
<CheckboxGroup aria-labelledby="terms-label" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="terms-error">
	<Label id="terms-label">{t("terms.label")}</Label>
	<Checkbox name="terms" value="accepted" required>{t("terms.accept")}</Checkbox>
	<FieldError id="terms-error">{t("terms.required")}</FieldError>
</CheckboxGroup>

rows.name: orientation
rows.description: Layout axis. Defaults to DEFAULT_ORIENTATION.

types.name: Orientation
types.description: Axis a group's checkboxes lay out along: a single column, or a single row.

checkbox.name: Checkbox
checkbox.definition:
A styled native checkbox: an `<input type="checkbox">` paired with a
decorative glyph box that renders its check or dash mark purely from the
input's own state, wrapped in a `<label>` so clicking or tapping anywhere
in the row — box, glyph, or label text alike — toggles the control.
checkbox.summary: A styled native checkbox: an `<input type="checkbox">` paired with a decorative glyph box that renders its check or dash mark purely from the input's own state, wrapped in a `<label>` so clicking or tapping anywhere in the row — box, glyph, or label text alike — toggles the control.

rows.name: role
rows.description: ARIA role override, restricted to what a checkbox input may carry.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Label content rendered after the box, inside the same native `<label>` wrapping the row — clicking any of it toggles the checkbox natively, with no separate `htmlFor`/`id` pair required.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this wrapper's internally composed elements.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

color-area.name: ColorArea
color-area.definition:
A two-dimensional saturation/brightness picking square for a given hue,
built from two overlaid native `<input type="range">` elements — one
horizontal for saturation, one rotated vertical for brightness — whose
native thumbs, each reshaped into a thin line, cross at the picked point.
color-area.summary: A two-dimensional saturation/brightness picking square for a given hue, built from two overlaid native `<input type="range">` elements — one horizontal for saturation, one rotated vertical for brightness — whose native thumbs, each reshaped into a thin line, cross at the picked point.
color-area.description:
Renders the root `<div>`'s picking-square background: literal `black`/`white`
gradient stops are the fixed brightness/saturation math primaries, and the
hue's `hsl()` composes through `bg()`, since it passes `(`-values unchanged.
examples:
<ColorArea aria-label={t("colorPicker.area")} hue={210} defaultSaturation={80} defaultValue={70}>
	<ColorArea.SaturationThumb aria-label={t("colorPicker.saturation")} />
	<ColorArea.ValueThumb aria-label={t("colorPicker.brightness")} />
</ColorArea>

rows.name: hue
rows.description: Hue, in degrees `0`–`360`, the square's background renders every reachable saturation/brightness combination for. Defaults to DEFAULT_HUE. Typically driven by a hue control alongside this one, re-rendering on change.

rows.name: saturation
rows.description: Current saturation (x-axis position), `0`–`100`, for a square whose position the consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultSaturation
rows.description: Starting saturation (x-axis position), `0`–`100`, for a square that never tracks its own position.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current brightness (y-axis position), `0`–`100`, for a square whose position the consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Starting brightness (y-axis position), `0`–`100`, for a square that never tracks its own position.

parts.name: ColorArea.SaturationThumb
parts.description: `direction` stays fixed left-to-right regardless of the page's own `dir`, matching the root gradient's physical axes; only this thumb's own line accepts pointer input, so elsewhere a click reaches the axis line beneath it.

parts.name: ColorArea.ValueThumb
parts.description: `writing-mode`/`direction` stay fixed regardless of the page's own `dir`, so this line travels block-end (black) to block-start, the low-at-the- bottom convention; pointer layering matches ColorArea.SaturationThumb.

color-field.name: ColorField
color-field.definition:
A labeled, described, and validated color field in one call: every id and
`aria-describedby` relationship comes from this instance's own stable
identifier, so the composed parts stay associated on their own. The preview
paints the resolved value at render time, so it matches the control on
first paint and on every server round-trip.
color-field.summary: A labeled, described, and validated color field in one call: every id and `aria-describedby` relationship comes from this instance's own stable identifier, so the composed parts stay associated on their own.
color-field.description:
Composes Label, an Input constrained by `format`'s native
`pattern`, a live ColorSwatch preview of the resolved value, and
any Description or FieldError, wired to this instance's own id.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the control's focus ring. Defaults to `"neutral"` when omitted.

rows.name: label
rows.description: The field's caption, rendered through Label and associated with the control through a native `for`/`id` relationship computed from this instance's own identifier.

rows.name: description
rows.description: Supporting copy rendered through Description beneath the control and referenced by the control's `aria-describedby`.

rows.name: errorMessage
rows.description: Validation message rendered through FieldError beneath the control, referenced by its `aria-describedby`; its presence alone marks `aria-invalid`. Inside a Form carrying `issues`, this prop wins.

rows.name: autoFocus
rows.description: Native `autofocus`. Defaults to `true` for the first invalid field of an enclosing Form's `issues`, so a server round-trip lands keyboard focus on the first problem while staying script-free.

rows.name: format
rows.description: Notation the control's `pattern` constrains typed entry to. Defaults to DEFAULT_FORMAT.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current value, as a literal color string in `format`'s notation, for a control a consumer tracks itself. This same string paints the preview directly.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Initial value, as a literal color string in `format`'s notation, for a control left to the platform's own uncontrolled state. This same string paints the preview directly whenever `value` is unset.

rows.name: placeholder
rows.description: Placeholder copy shown while the control is empty.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the control required for its enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the control inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks the control's value fixed, while keeping it focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this wrapper's internally composed elements.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role for the control's keyboard focus ring, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

types.name: Format
types.description: Notation the control's typed value is constrained to through its native `pattern`: `"hex"` for `#rgb`/`#rrggbb` and their alpha forms, `"rgb"` for `rgb()`/`rgba()`, and `"hsl"` for `hsl()`/`hsla()`.

color-picker.name: ColorPicker
color-picker.definition:
A labeled color field composing ColorField's plain fallback with
an optional ColorPicker.Group trigger row and
ColorPicker.Dialog picking surface swapped in via `children`.
color-picker.summary: A labeled color field composing ColorField's plain fallback with an optional ColorPicker.Group trigger row and ColorPicker.Dialog picking surface swapped in via `children`.
color-picker.description:
Renders ColorPicker's root: ColorField's plain fallback
when `children` is unset, or the trigger-and-panel layout composed from
ColorPicker.Group and ColorPicker.Dialog otherwise.
examples:
<ColorPicker>
	<Label htmlFor="brandColor">{t("form.brandColor.label")}</Label>
	<ColorPicker.Group>
		<Input id="brandColor" type="text" name="brandColor" defaultValue="#3b82f6" />
		<ColorPicker.Trigger
			commandfor="brandColor-panel"
			command="toggle-popover"
			aria-label={t("form.brandColor.toggle")}
			value="#3b82f6"
		/>
	</ColorPicker.Group>
	<ColorPicker.Dialog id="brandColor-panel">
		{...the picking surface — see ColorPicker.Dialog's own doc comment}
	</ColorPicker.Dialog>
</ColorPicker>

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the fallback field's focus ring. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: label
rows.description: The fallback field's caption, rendered through ColorField. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: description
rows.description: Supporting copy beneath the fallback field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: errorMessage
rows.description: Validation message beneath the fallback field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: format
rows.description: Notation the fallback field's typed entry is constrained to. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form, read only by the fallback field.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current value, as a literal color string, for a fallback field a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Initial value, as a literal color string, for a fallback field left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: placeholder
rows.description: Placeholder copy shown while the fallback field is empty.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the fallback field required for its enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the fallback field inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks the fallback field's value fixed, while keeping it focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint for the fallback field.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the fallback field's internally composed parts. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The trigger-and-panel layout — typically a `Label`, ColorPicker.Group, and ColorPicker.Dialog — rendered in place of ColorField's plain fallback. Unset renders that fallback.

parts.name: ColorPicker.Group
parts.description: Renders ColorPicker's control row: a plain flex host laying the field's own control and ColorPicker.Trigger side by side, with a keyboard focus ring on the whole row the moment focus lands anywhere inside.

parts.name: ColorPicker.Trigger
parts.description: Renders ColorPicker's trailing trigger: a `<button>` housing a ColorSwatch that fills it as a live preview, wired via `commandfor`/`command="toggle-popover"` to ColorPicker.Dialog's `id`.

rows.name: value
rows.description: The color this trigger previews, already resolved to a literal CSS color value — the same value its inner ColorSwatch paints. Required, since a trigger with nothing to preview has no reason to render.

rows.name: shape
rows.description: Shape variant for the inner ColorSwatch, mirrored onto the button host so its own corners match. Defaults to DEFAULT_TRIGGER_SHAPE.

parts.name: ColorPicker.Dialog
parts.description: Renders ColorPicker's picking surface: a Popover, defaulting `placement` to bottom-start and `role` to `"dialog"`, padding whatever picking controls a consumer composes as `children` in a single column.

color-slider.name: ColorSlider
color-slider.definition:
A single-channel color control on a native `<input type="range">`, pairing
a track painting the channel's gradient with a thumb reporting the current
value and an `<output>` for its formatted display. The root shares the
resolved channel, range, and value with every part through context.
color-slider.summary: A single-channel color control on a native `<input type="range">`, pairing a track painting the channel's gradient with a thumb reporting the current value and an `<output>` for its formatted display.
color-slider.description:
Renders the root host: a `<div>` stacking its children with a small gap,
resolving the channel, range, and value into component context and
mirroring the channel onto its own `data-channel` attribute.
examples:
<ColorSlider channel="alpha" min={0} max={1} defaultValue={1}>
	<ColorSlider.Track hue={210}>
		<ColorSlider.Thumb aria-label={t("colorPicker.alpha")} />
	</ColorSlider.Track>
</ColorSlider>

rows.name: channel
rows.description: The single channel this instance edits.

rows.name: min
rows.description: Lower bound of the channel's range. Defaults to DEFAULT_MIN.

rows.name: max
rows.description: Upper bound of the channel's range. Defaults to `channel`'s entry in DEFAULT_MAX_BY_CHANNEL.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current value, for an instance whose value the consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Starting value, for an instance that never tracks its own value.

parts.name: ColorSlider.Track
parts.description: Renders the visual track: a `position: relative` `<div>` painting its whole length with the gradient the nearest ancestor ColorSlider's `data-channel` attribute selects, over a checkerboard backdrop.

rows.name: hue
rows.description: The color's current hue, in degrees `0`–`360`, read into TRACK_HUE_PROPERTY at render time so a `"saturation"`, `"lightness"`, or `"alpha"` track's gradient matches it. Defaults to DEFAULT_HUE.

parts.name: ColorSlider.Thumb
parts.description: Renders the interactive thumb: a native `<input type="range">` reset to cover its enclosing ColorSlider.Track's entire box, so drag, arrow-key, and click-to-jump behavior spans the track's whole length.

parts.name: ColorSlider.Output
parts.description: Renders a live readout: a native `<output>` reporting the formatted value passed as `children`.

types.name: Channel
types.description: The single color channel one ColorSlider instance edits.

color-swatch-picker.name: ColorSwatchPicker
color-swatch-picker.definition:
A set of mutually exclusive color options built from native `<input
type="radio">` controls sharing one grouping name, rendered as a
`role="radiogroup"` host wrapping ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch
instances styled from each input's own `:checked` state.
color-swatch-picker.summary: A set of mutually exclusive color options built from native `<input type="radio">` controls sharing one grouping name, rendered as a `role="radiogroup"` host wrapping ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch instances styled from each input's own `:checked` state.
color-swatch-picker.description:
Renders the group host: a `role="radiogroup"` `<div>` laying its
ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch options out in a wrapping row, sharing its
`name` through context so each option defaults to the group's own identifier.
examples:
<ColorSwatchPicker aria-label={t("form.accentColor.label")} name="accentColor">
	<ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch value="#ef4444" aria-label={t("color.red")} />
	<ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch value="#3b82f6" aria-label={t("color.blue")} defaultChecked />
	<ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch value="#22c55e" aria-label={t("color.green")} />
</ColorSwatchPicker>

<ColorSwatchPicker aria-label={t("form.brandColor.label")}>
	<ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch value="#f97316" aria-label={t("color.orange")} shape="circle" size="lg" />
	<ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch value="#a855f7" aria-label={t("color.purple")} shape="circle" size="lg" />
</ColorSwatchPicker>

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native grouping name shared by every ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch nested inside. Defaults to the group's own stable instance id when omitted.

parts.name: ColorSwatchPicker.Swatch
parts.description: Renders a single option: a hidden `<input type="radio">` paired with a ColorSwatch indicator, styled through `precededBy()` since a bare element-first selector here would serialize as a declaration, not a match.

rows.name: value
rows.description: The color this option submits and previews, already resolved to a literal CSS color value — the same value ColorSwatch paints its indicator with and submits with the enclosing form.

rows.name: "aria-label"
rows.description: Accessible name announced for this option in place of visible text — a color's name, for instance. Required, since the indicator identifies the option to assistive technology through this text alone.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native grouping name for this option's underlying input. Defaults to the name provided by the nearest ancestor ColorSwatchPicker — set this only to opt a single option out of its group's shared name.

rows.name: shape
rows.description: The indicator's shape variant, forwarded to ColorSwatch.

rows.name: size
rows.description: The indicator's size variant, forwarded to ColorSwatch.

rows.name: defaultChecked
rows.description: Whether this option starts selected, for a form that never tracks selection itself.

rows.name: checked
rows.description: Whether this option is selected, for a form that tracks selection itself.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Whether this option is inert and excluded from the group's tab order.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the enclosing native radio group as requiring one option selected.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the option's hidden `input` and its ColorSwatch indicator, layered after each part's own built-in styling. The `mix` prop styles the option's outer `<label>` host.

color-swatch.name: ColorSwatch
color-swatch.definition:
A static preview box rendering one color value as a filled, shaped
swatch, backed by a fixed checkerboard so a translucent value always
reads correctly against whatever sits behind it on the page rather than
blending invisibly away. The value paints through two stacked layers: a
checkerboard base and a color fill on top, clipped together to a circular,
square, or softly rounded shape at one of three fixed sizes. Every other
color preview in this component family composes this box for its own
preview instead of redrawing the checkerboard-plus-fill technique itself.
color-swatch.summary: A static preview box rendering one color value as a filled, shaped swatch, backed by a fixed checkerboard so a translucent value always reads correctly against whatever sits behind it on the page rather than blending invisibly away.
color-swatch.description:
Renders a fixed-size `<span>` that paints `value` through a local
`--ui-color-swatch-value` custom property, layered over a `::before`
checkerboard so any transparency in `value` reads correctly.

rows.name: value
rows.description: The color to preview, already resolved to a literal CSS value — a hex string, `rgb()`/`hsl()`/`oklch()` function, or named color. Required, since a swatch with nothing to preview has no reason to render.

rows.name: shape
rows.description: Shape variant. Defaults to DEFAULT_SHAPE.

rows.name: size
rows.description: Size variant. Defaults to DEFAULT_SIZE.

types.name: Shape
types.description: Shape variant controlling the swatch's corner rounding: `"circle"` renders a fully rounded disc, `"square"` renders sharp corners, and `"rounded"` renders a softly rounded square.

types.name: Size
types.description: Size variant controlling the swatch's rendered dimensions.

color-wheel.name: ColorWheel
color-wheel.definition:
A circular hue picker. Hue's natural domain is an angle swept around a
circle, so the pointer math is polar: a center point and an angle in, a
hue out. A single native `<input type="range">` carries every value this
control reports; `colorWheelDrag()` reshapes the root into a ring when a
consumer attaches it through the root's `mix` prop.
color-wheel.description:
Renders a root `<div>` around a single `<input type="range">` across
hue's `0`–`360` domain, carrying every accessibility and form semantic
this wheel exposes; `colorWheelDrag()` enables the ring rendering.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current hue, in degrees `0`–`360`, for a wheel a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Starting hue, in degrees `0`–`360`, for a wheel left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: step
rows.description: Degrees a single keypress moves the value by. Defaults to DEFAULT_STEP.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form.

rows.name: form
rows.description: Native `id` of the form the underlying hue input associates with, when it sits outside that form's own markup.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the underlying hue input inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this wrapper's internally composed hue input.

combobox.name: ComboBox
combobox.definition:
A single-line text control paired with a native list of suggested values: a
ComboBox.Group row housing the ComboBox.Input control and a
trailing ComboBox.Button disclosure glyph, all stacked beneath a
caption or above supporting copy in a single column with a small gap. The
text control builds on Input for its box, color, and interaction
states, and pairs with a plain `<datalist>` of `<option>`s through its own
`list` attribute — the browser renders and filters that list entirely on
its own, with no styling opportunity across the suggestions themselves.
combobox.summary: A single-line text control paired with a native list of suggested values: a ComboBox.Group row housing the ComboBox.Input control and a trailing ComboBox.Button disclosure glyph, all stacked beneath a caption or above supporting copy in a single column with a small gap.
combobox.description:
Renders a plain host stacking this control's compound parts — a caption,
the ComboBox.Group row, a `<datalist>` of suggested values, and
supporting copy — in a single column with a small gap between them.
examples:
<ComboBox>
	<Label htmlFor="fruit">{t("form.fruit.label")}</Label>
	<ComboBox.Group>
		<ComboBox.Input id="fruit" name="fruit" list="fruit-options" />
		<ComboBox.Button aria-label={t("form.fruit.toggle")} />
	</ComboBox.Group>
	<datalist id="fruit-options">
		<option value="Apple" />
		<option value="Banana" />
	</datalist>
</ComboBox>

parts.name: ComboBox.Group
parts.description: Renders ComboBox's control row: a plain flex host laying ComboBox.Input and ComboBox.Button side by side, the button pulled back over the input's padding so they read as one field.

parts.name: ComboBox.Input
parts.description: Renders ComboBox's text control: an Input that grows to fill its row, reserves inline-end padding for ComboBox.Button's glyph, and carries every Input interaction state unchanged.

parts.name: ComboBox.Button
parts.description: Renders ComboBox's trailing disclosure glyph: a native `<button>` pulled back over ComboBox.Input's padding so it reads as part of the same field, its chevron marked `aria-hidden` since it carries no text.

command.name: Command
command.definition:
A bordered panel for searching and choosing among a list of actions:
Command.Input holds the query row, Command.List scrolls
through Command.Item rows, and Command.Empty holds a
message for when nothing matches. Its baseline rendering is a plain, fully
visible list of options, styled and ready to compose; the as-you-type
filtering and match highlighting a search experience needs arrive through
a separate opt-in behavior a consumer attaches.
command.summary: A bordered panel for searching and choosing among a list of actions: Command.Input holds the query row, Command.List scrolls through Command.Item rows, and Command.Empty holds a message for when nothing matches.
command.description:
Renders the panel's root host: a bordered, rounded, elevated `<div>`
stacking its compound parts in a column, clipping Command.List's
scrolled content to the panel's own rounded corners.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The panel's compound parts: Command.Input, Command.List, Command.Empty.

parts.name: Command.Input
parts.description: Renders the panel's query row: a `<div>` bordered along its block-end edge wrapping a native `<input>` sized to the row's full padding and height, marked `data-command-input` for a paired filter mixin to read.

parts.name: Command.List
parts.description: Renders the panel's scrollable option region: a `<div>` carrying the `listbox` role, capped at a fixed block size, its small inline padding leaving room for a selected Command.Item's own rounded corners.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The Command.Item rows (and, once nothing matches, Command.Empty) to scroll through.

parts.name: Command.Item
parts.description: Renders a single row: a `<div>` carrying the `option` role, its `value` mirrored onto `data-value` for a paired filter behavior to read.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Plain-text value identifying this row's content. A paired filter behavior matches typed text against this value directly, so it stays required even when the visible content is already plain text.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's visible content: a label, and optionally a leading icon or trailing hint.

parts.name: Command.Empty
parts.description: Renders the panel's no-match message: a centered, muted passage of small text filling Command.List's content area, carrying a `data-command-empty` marker a paired filter behavior reads to toggle it.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.definition:
A convenience wrapper composing a two-control confirmation prompt in one
call: an AlertDialog panel prefilled with a heading, an optional
supporting passage, and a cancel/confirm control pair, so a single
consequential decision needs no compound assembly of its own. The
confirming control defaults to the semantic danger tone, keeping an
irreversible action behind an explicit confirmation step in that tone.
confirm.summary: A convenience wrapper composing a two-control confirmation prompt in one call: an AlertDialog panel prefilled with a heading, an optional supporting passage, and a cancel/confirm control pair, so a single consequential decision needs no compound assembly of its own.
confirm.description:
Composes AlertDialog into a confirmation prompt, wiring title and
description ids to `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`. Omit
Confirm.Props.form to close on confirm, or pass it to submit a real `<form>` instead.
examples:
<Button commandfor="confirm-delete" command="show-modal" color="danger">{t("project.delete")}</Button>
<Confirm
	id="confirm-delete"
	title={t("project.deleteTitle")}
	description={t("project.deleteDescription")}
	confirmLabel={t("actions.delete")}
	cancelLabel={t("actions.cancel")}
/>

<Confirm
	id="revoke-session"
	title={t("session.revokeTitle")}
	confirmLabel={t("actions.revoke")}
	cancelLabel={t("actions.cancel")}
	form={{ action: revokeUrl, fields: <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value={token} /> }}
/>

rows.name: id
rows.description: Stable identifier the panel renders as its own `id`; a trigger elsewhere on the page targets it via `commandfor`/`command="show-modal"`, and the cancel and confirm controls point back at it automatically.

rows.name: title
rows.description: The panel's heading, rendered through AlertDialog.Title.

rows.name: description
rows.description: Supporting copy rendered through AlertDialog.Description beneath the title. Omit to render no description.

rows.name: confirmLabel
rows.description: Label for the confirming control, rendered through AlertDialog.Action.

rows.name: cancelLabel
rows.description: Label for the control that backs out without confirming, rendered through AlertDialog.Cancel.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color for the confirming control. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: form
rows.description: Submission the confirming control performs. Omitting it leaves confirming as a close-only action for the page to react to; setting it submits a real form instead.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this wrapper's internally composed elements.

context-menu.name: ContextMenu
context-menu.definition:
A menu surface that opens at a right-click's pointer position, composing
Menu's popover styling and `role="menu"` wiring directly so its
rows read and behave exactly like a standard menu's. Adds the
ContextMenu.Trigger wrapper a pointer gesture opens the surface
against, plus the grouped-row parts — ContextMenu.Group,
ContextMenu.Label, and ContextMenu.Shortcut — a context
menu's denser row layout tends to need.
context-menu.summary: A menu surface that opens at a right-click's pointer position, composing Menu's popover styling and `role="menu"` wiring directly so its rows read and behave exactly like a standard menu's.
context-menu.description:
Renders Menu unchanged; positioning against the pointer is handled
entirely by the `contextMenu()` mixin a consuming island applies to
ContextMenu.Trigger, while every nested row stays a real, tab-reachable `<a>` or `<button>`.

parts.name: ContextMenu.Trigger
parts.description: Renders ContextMenu.TriggerProps.children inside a plain `<div>`, the area a pointer gesture opens the paired ContextMenu against.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The content the pointer gesture opens ContextMenu against.

parts.name: ContextMenu.Group
parts.description: Renders ContextMenu.GroupProps.children as one labeled run of rows: Section restyled with a divider above every group but the first.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The group's rows, typically a ContextMenu.Label followed by a run of ContextMenu.Items.

parts.name: ContextMenu.Label
parts.description: Renders ContextMenu.LabelProps.children as a ContextMenu.Group's small, muted heading, sized and spaced to sit directly above the group's first row for a dense row of actions.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The group's visible label text.

parts.name: ContextMenu.SubTrigger
parts.description: Renders a row that opens a nested ContextMenu.SubContent surface: Menu.Item restyled with inline-end padding for a trailing chevron icon; point `commandfor` at the nested surface's `id` with `command="toggle-popover"`.

parts.name: ContextMenu.SubContent
parts.description: Renders a nested surface opened by a ContextMenu.SubTrigger row: ContextMenu itself, defaulting `placement` to DEFAULT_SUB_PLACEMENT since a nested row conventionally opens beside itself.

parts.name: ContextMenu.Shortcut
parts.description: Renders ContextMenu.ShortcutProps.children as a row's trailing keyboard-shortcut hint: pushed to the row's inline end and muted, reading as supplementary detail alongside the row's primary label.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The shortcut hint text, typically a key combination like "⌘⇧D".

date-field.name: DateField
date-field.definition:
A convenience wrapper composing a labeled, described, and validated date
field in one call: a caption through Label, a native
`<input type="date">` styled through Input, an optional supporting
passage through Description, and an optional validation message
through FieldError. Every id and `aria-describedby` relationship
between the parts is computed from this instance's own stable identifier,
leaving no id bookkeeping to the consumer.
date-field.summary: A convenience wrapper composing a labeled, described, and validated date field in one call: a caption through Label, a native `<input type="date">` styled through Input, an optional supporting passage through Description, and an optional validation message through FieldError.
date-field.description:
Renders a complete date field in one call, stacking Label,
Input, and, when supplied, Description and FieldError.
An invalid state — from `errorMessage` or an explicit `aria-invalid` override — recolors the border and ring to the semantic danger tone regardless of `color`.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the control's focus ring. Defaults to `"neutral"` when omitted.

rows.name: label
rows.description: The field's caption, rendered through Label and associated with the control through a native `for`/`id` relationship computed from this instance's own identifier.

rows.name: description
rows.description: Supporting copy rendered through Description beneath the control and referenced by the control's `aria-describedby`. Omit to render no description.

rows.name: errorMessage
rows.description: Validation message rendered through FieldError beneath the control; its presence alone marks `aria-invalid` unless set explicitly. Inside a Form carrying `issues`, an explicit value still wins over the field's own by-`name` lookup.

rows.name: autoFocus
rows.description: Native `autofocus`. Defaults to `true` for the first invalid field of an enclosing Form's `issues`, landing keyboard focus on the problem after a server round-trip; pass it explicitly to override for this field.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a control a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Initial value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a control left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: min
rows.description: Earliest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form.

rows.name: max
rows.description: Latest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form.

rows.name: step
rows.description: Granularity, in days, the control's value must fall on.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the control required for its enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the control inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks the control's value fixed, while keeping it focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint, e.g. `"bday"`.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this wrapper's internally composed elements.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role for the control's keyboard focus ring, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

date-picker.name: DatePicker
date-picker.definition:
A labeled date field building on DateField for its plain fallback,
extended with a DatePicker.Group row and a trigger
DatePicker.Button for composing a DatePicker.Dialog —
a Popover-hosted calendar surface — alongside it. Composing
DatePicker.Group and DatePicker.Dialog as children swaps in
that richer trigger-and-calendar layout in place of the plain fallback
field; leaving `children` unset keeps the fallback on its own, a complete,
keyboard-operable control with no composed surface at all.
date-picker.summary: A labeled date field building on DateField for its plain fallback, extended with a DatePicker.Group row and a trigger DatePicker.Button for composing a DatePicker.Dialog — a Popover-hosted calendar surface — alongside it.
examples:
<DatePicker>
	<Label htmlFor="startDate">{t("form.startDate.label")}</Label>
	<DatePicker.Group>
		<Input id="startDate" type="date" name="startDate" />
		<DatePicker.Button
			commandfor="startDate-calendar"
			command="toggle-popover"
			aria-label={t("form.startDate.toggle")}
		/>
	</DatePicker.Group>
	<DatePicker.Dialog id="startDate-calendar">
		<Calendar aria-label={monthLabel}>
			<Calendar.Header>
				<Calendar.PreviousButton aria-label={t("calendar.previous")} />
				<Calendar.Heading>{monthLabel}</Calendar.Heading>
				<Calendar.NextButton aria-label={t("calendar.next")} />
			</Calendar.Header>
			<Calendar.Grid aria-label={monthLabel}>...</Calendar.Grid>
		</Calendar>
	</DatePicker.Dialog>
</DatePicker>

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the fallback field's focus ring. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: label
rows.description: The fallback field's caption, rendered through DateField. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: description
rows.description: Supporting copy beneath the fallback field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: errorMessage
rows.description: Validation message beneath the fallback field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form, read only by the fallback field.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Current value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a fallback field a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: defaultValue
rows.description: Initial value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a fallback field left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: min
rows.description: Earliest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read only by the fallback field.

rows.name: max
rows.description: Latest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read only by the fallback field.

rows.name: step
rows.description: Granularity, in days, the fallback field's value must fall on.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the fallback field required for its enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the fallback field inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks the fallback field's value fixed, while keeping it focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint for the fallback field, e.g. `"bday"`.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the fallback field's internally composed parts. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The trigger-and-calendar layout — typically a `Label`, DatePicker.Group, and DatePicker.Dialog — rendered in place of the plain fallback field, leaving every field above unread.

parts.name: DatePicker.Group
parts.description: Renders DatePicker's control row: a plain flex host laying the field's own control and DatePicker.Button out side by side.

parts.name: DatePicker.Button
parts.description: Renders DatePicker's trailing trigger: a native `<button>` pulled back over the row's trailing space so it reads as part of the same field.

parts.name: DatePicker.Dialog
parts.description: Renders DatePicker's calendar surface: a Popover whose `placement` defaults to reading down and start-ward from its invoker, and whose `role` defaults to `"dialog"`.

date-range-picker.name: DateRangePicker
date-range-picker.definition:
A paired-field date range control building on DateField for its
plain fallback — independent start-date and end-date fields, each fully
labeled, described, and validated on its own — extended with a
DateRangePicker.Group row and a trigger
DateRangePicker.Button for composing a
DateRangePicker.Dialog calendar surface alongside it. Leaving
`children` unset keeps the fallback pair on its own, complete and
keyboard-operable with no composed surface at all.
date-range-picker.summary: A paired-field date range control building on DateField for its plain fallback — independent start-date and end-date fields, each fully labeled, described, and validated on its own — extended with a DateRangePicker.Group row and a trigger DateRangePicker.Button for composing a DateRangePicker.Dialog calendar surface alongside it.
date-range-picker.description:
Renders DateRangePicker's root. Leaving `children` unset renders
two independent DateField instances side by side under a native
`role="group"`, each aligned to its own start edge so a validation message under one never shifts the other's label; composing DateRangePicker.Group and DateRangePicker.Dialog as `children` instead renders the richer layout and leaves every field above unread.
examples:
<DateRangePicker>
	<Label htmlFor="tripStart">{t("form.trip.label")}</Label>
	<DateRangePicker.Group>
		<Input id="tripStart" type="date" name="tripStart" />
		<Input id="tripEnd" type="date" name="tripEnd" />
		<DateRangePicker.Button
			commandfor="trip-calendar"
			command="toggle-popover"
			aria-label={t("form.trip.toggle")}
		/>
	</DateRangePicker.Group>
	<DateRangePicker.Dialog id="trip-calendar">
		<RangeCalendar aria-label={monthLabel}>
			<RangeCalendar.Header>
				<RangeCalendar.PreviousButton aria-label={t("calendar.previous")} />
				<RangeCalendar.Heading>{monthLabel}</RangeCalendar.Heading>
				<RangeCalendar.NextButton aria-label={t("calendar.next")} />
			</RangeCalendar.Header>
			<RangeCalendar.Grid aria-label={monthLabel}>...</RangeCalendar.Grid>
		</RangeCalendar>
	</DateRangePicker.Dialog>
</DateRangePicker>

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the fallback pair's focus rings. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: startLabel
rows.description: The start-date field's caption, rendered through DateField. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: endLabel
rows.description: The end-date field's caption, rendered through DateField. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: startDescription
rows.description: Supporting copy beneath the start-date field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: endDescription
rows.description: Supporting copy beneath the end-date field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: startErrorMessage
