rows.description: Validation message beneath the start-date field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: endErrorMessage
rows.description: Validation message beneath the end-date field. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: startName
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form for the start-date field.

rows.name: endName
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form for the end-date field.

rows.name: startValue
rows.description: Current start-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a fallback pair a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: endValue
rows.description: Current end-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a fallback pair a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: startDefaultValue
rows.description: Initial start-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a fallback pair left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: endDefaultValue
rows.description: Initial end-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a fallback pair left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: min
rows.description: Earliest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read by both of the fallback pair's fields.

rows.name: max
rows.description: Latest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read by both of the fallback pair's fields.

rows.name: step
rows.description: Granularity, in days, both of the fallback pair's values must fall on.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks both of the fallback pair's fields required for their enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks both of the fallback pair's fields inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks both of the fallback pair's fields' values fixed, while keeping them focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint for both of the fallback pair's fields.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the fallback pair's internally composed DateField instances. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The trigger-and-calendar layout — typically a `Label`, DateRangePicker.Group, and DateRangePicker.Dialog — rendered in place of the paired fallback fields, leaving every field above unread when set.

description.name: Description
description.definition:
A short passage of supporting copy beneath a form control, styled at the library's default text size and the neutral muted foreground color. It renders as a native `

` so a consumer can wire its `id` into the control's `aria-describedby`, giving assistive technology a spoken hint, format requirement, or constraint alongside the control's label.
description.summary: A short passage of supporting copy beneath a form control, styled at the library's default text size and the neutral muted foreground color.
description.description:
Renders its children inside a `

` sized and colored as a small run of supporting copy: the library's default text size paired with the neutral muted foreground color, placed after a control inside a field wrapper as a format hint or constraint note.

dialog.name: Dialog
dialog.definition:
A modal surface built on the native `<dialog>` element, opened and closed
declaratively through Invoker Commands (`commandfor`/`command`) instead of
a JavaScript-tracked open state. Compound parts cover a header, title,
description, footer, and a dismiss control, so a page composes only the
pieces a given dialog needs.
dialog.summary: A modal surface built on the native `<dialog>` element, opened and closed declaratively through Invoker Commands (`commandfor`/`command`) instead of a JavaScript-tracked open state.
dialog.description:
Renders the dialog panel as a native `<dialog>` host, its `::backdrop`
tinted and, where supported, blurred to dim the page behind it. The panel
declares the `ui-dialog` named container so Dialog.Header and Dialog.Footer can size against the panel's own width; Invoker Commands open and close it declaratively — a trigger elsewhere points `commandfor` at this element's `id` with `command="show-modal"`, and any control inside, including Dialog.Close, points `commandfor` at that same `id` with `command="close"`.
examples:
<Button commandfor="confirm-delete" command="show-modal">{t("project.delete")}</Button>
<Dialog id="confirm-delete" aria-labelledby="confirm-delete-title">
	<Dialog.Header>
		<Dialog.Title id="confirm-delete-title">{t("project.deleteTitle")}</Dialog.Title>
		<Dialog.Description>{t("project.deleteDescription")}</Dialog.Description>
	</Dialog.Header>
	<Dialog.Footer>
		<Button commandfor="confirm-delete" command="close" color="danger">{t("actions.delete")}</Button>
	</Dialog.Footer>
	<Dialog.Close commandfor="confirm-delete" aria-label={t("actions.close")} />
</Dialog>

rows.name: children
rows.description: The panel's compound parts: Dialog.Header, Dialog.Footer, Dialog.Close, or any other content.

parts.name: Dialog.Header
parts.description: Renders Dialog.HeaderProps.children as the panel's header slot: a column stacking Dialog.Title and Dialog.Description, centered while narrow and start-aligned (flipping under `dir="rtl"`) once the panel's own `ui-dialog` container grows past `40rem`.

parts.name: Dialog.Title
parts.description: Renders Dialog.TitleProps.children as the panel's heading, inside the native heading element matching the nearest ambient heading level — `<h1>` by default — sized and weighted as the panel's most prominent line of text at every level.

parts.name: Dialog.Description
parts.description:
Renders Dialog.DescriptionProps.children as the panel's supporting copy, in a native `

` set to the panel's muted foreground color so it reads as secondary to Dialog.Title.

parts.name: Dialog.Footer
parts.description: Renders Dialog.FooterProps.children as the panel's action row: a column of stacked, full-width controls while the panel is narrow, switching to a single end-aligned row past the panel's own `40rem` container mark.

parts.name: Dialog.Close
parts.description: Renders a dismiss control for the ancestor Dialog named by `commandfor`: a small, ghost-styled Button with a fixed "X" glyph, pinned to the panel's corner.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of the ancestor Dialog this button dismisses.

rows.name: command
rows.description: Invoker Commands verb dispatched to the target Dialog. Defaults to `"close"`.

rows.name: "aria-label"
rows.description: Accessible label for the icon-only control — required, since the button carries no visible text for assistive technology to read.

disclosure.name: Disclosure
disclosure.definition:
A single expand/collapse section built on the native `<details>` and
`<summary>` elements, so the show/hide state, keyboard handling, and
find-in-page behavior all come from the platform itself.
`Disclosure.Trigger` is the always-visible `<summary>` label and
`Disclosure.Panel` is the content it reveals; `Disclosure.Group` stacks
several disclosures into one bordered list.
disclosure.summary: A single expand/collapse section built on the native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements, so the show/hide state, keyboard handling, and find-in-page behavior all come from the platform itself.
disclosure.description:
Renders the section's `<details>` host, revealing
Disclosure.Panel's content while `open`. The `::details-content`
block-size transition is a progressive enhancement over the native toggle.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The section's compound parts: Disclosure.Trigger followed by Disclosure.Panel.

parts.name: Disclosure.Header
parts.description: Renders Disclosure.HeaderProps.children as an accessible heading at the ambient level, nested directly inside Disclosure.Trigger, since `<summary>` must stay `<details>`'s direct child.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The trigger's label text, exposed as a heading for assistive technology.

parts.name: Disclosure.Trigger
parts.description: Renders Disclosure.TriggerProps.children inside a native `<summary>` with its marker suppressed so a consumer supplies its own indicator.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The always-visible label, typically plain text or Disclosure.Header.

parts.name: Disclosure.Panel
parts.description: Renders Disclosure.PanelProps.children in a `<div>` positioned after Disclosure.Trigger, all `<details>` needs to treat it as the collapsible body.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The content revealed while the section is open.

parts.name: Disclosure.Group
parts.description: Renders Disclosure.GroupProps.children as a bordered, rounded list of Disclosure sections sharing one divider between them.

rows.name: children
rows.description: One or more Disclosure sections to stack into a single bordered list.

drawer.name: Drawer
drawer.definition:
A preset of Dialog docked flush against one physical edge of the
viewport, sized to fill that edge and sliding into place from it on open,
back out on close. Every other detail — the dimming, blurrable
`::backdrop`, the `ui-dialog` named container its compound parts query,
and the missing-`id` dev-mode contract check — carries over from
Dialog, since this component composes it directly.
drawer.summary: A preset of Dialog docked flush against one physical edge of the viewport, sized to fill that edge and sliding into place from it on open, back out on close.
drawer.description:
Renders Dialog pinned to one edge of the viewport, animating a
`transform` off the native `open` attribute so `@starting-style` can
animate the close; a `mix` prop composes alongside this placement styling.
examples:
<Button commandfor="cart" command="show-modal">{t("cart.open")}</Button>
<Drawer id="cart" placement="right" aria-labelledby="cart-title">
	<Drawer.Header>
		<Drawer.Title id="cart-title">{t("cart.title")}</Drawer.Title>
	</Drawer.Header>
	<Drawer.Close commandfor="cart" aria-label={t("actions.close")} />
</Drawer>

rows.name: placement
rows.description: Physical edge of the viewport to dock against and slide in from. Defaults to DEFAULT_PLACEMENT.

types.name: Placement
types.description: Physical edge of the viewport the panel docks against and slides in from.

drop-indicator.name: DropIndicator
drop-indicator.definition:
A thin bar rendered in the gap between two items of a reorderable list,
marking where a dragged item will land. It sits in a muted ring tone at
rest and switches to the primary solid color once it becomes the
pointer's current drop target, with the surrounding list's own reorder
interaction deciding when it appears and which gap it marks.
drop-indicator.summary: A thin bar rendered in the gap between two items of a reorderable list, marking where a dragged item will land.
drop-indicator.description:
Renders a full-width, hairline-thick, fully rounded bar shaped for the gap
between two items in a reorderable list. Its color follows the host's
`data-drop-target` attribute: muted at rest, solid as the active target.

rows.name: isDropTarget
rows.description: Whether this bar marks the pointer's current drop target. Renders the host's `data-drop-target` attribute when `true`, switching the bar to its active color. Defaults to DEFAULT_IS_DROP_TARGET.

drop-zone.name: DropZone
drop-zone.definition:
A styled drop target for files: a dashed, centered surface wrapping a
native `<input type="file">`, so picking a file through the platform's own
file picker works the moment the markup renders, with no script involved.
Its decorative content — an icon, an instructional caption, or both —
renders inside the same `<label>` that wraps the input, giving the input
its accessible name through the platform's own label association.
drop-zone.summary: A styled drop target for files: a dashed, centered surface wrapping a native `<input type="file">`, so picking a file through the platform's own file picker works the moment the markup renders, with no script involved.
drop-zone.description:
Renders a native `<input type="file">` wrapped in a `<label>` styled as a
dashed, centered drop surface; a paired drag-and-drop mixin toggles the
`data-drop-target` attribute this surface's styling reacts to.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form.

rows.name: accept
rows.description: Comma-separated list of accepted MIME types or file extensions.

rows.name: multiple
rows.description: Whether more than one file may be chosen at once.

rows.name: capture
rows.description: Requests a specific camera where a mobile browser's picker offers one.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the control required for its enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks the control inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The zone's visible content — an icon, an instructional caption, or both — rendered inside the `<label>` that wraps the file input, so clicking it opens the picker and names the input via label association.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this component's internally composed input.

empty.name: Empty
empty.definition:
A placeholder for a section that currently has nothing to show — a
dashed-bordered panel that composes an icon, a title, a description, and
an action into one empty-state layout. The compound parts let a consumer
include only the pieces a given empty state needs.
empty.summary: A placeholder for a section that currently has nothing to show — a dashed-bordered panel that composes an icon, a title, a description, and an action into one empty-state layout.
empty.description:
Renders the empty-state panel: a dashed-bordered column tinted to the
color role in Empty.Props.color. Its compound parts inherit that
color through `currentcolor`.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic tone of the panel. Default: `"neutral"`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The panel's compound parts: Empty.Icon, Empty.Title, Empty.Description, Empty.Action, or any other content.

parts.name: Empty.Icon
parts.description: Renders Empty.IconProps.children as the icon well: a fully rounded, tinted badge framing an icon graphic hidden from assistive technology, since Empty.Title's text already names the state.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Icon graphic rendered inside the icon well.

parts.name: Empty.Title
parts.description: Renders Empty.TitleProps.children as the empty state's heading, in the native heading element matching its ambient `HeadingScope` depth (or `<h1>` unscoped), sized as the panel's primary text regardless of level.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Heading copy for the empty state.

parts.name: Empty.Description
parts.description:
Renders Empty.DescriptionProps.children as the empty state's supporting copy, in a native `

` set to seventy percent of the panel's current text color so it reads as secondary to Empty.Title.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Supporting copy elaborating on the empty state.

parts.name: Empty.Action
parts.description: Renders Empty.ActionProps.children as the empty state's call-to-action slot, spaced a touch below the text above it.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Call-to-action content, typically a button or link.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic tone driving the panel's border, tint, and foreground color through the `--ui-*` variables for that color.

field-error.name: FieldError
field-error.definition:
A native form field's validation message, styled at a small size in the
danger foreground color. Its host carries a stable id — its own
`handle.id` unless a consumer supplies one — ready for a field's control
to reference through `aria-describedby`, and a `data-field-error` marker
that lets a validation script locate this slot through that same
`aria-describedby` list regardless of where it sits in the DOM. It
is the foundational error slot every field wrapper composes alongside a
label and a control.
field-error.summary: A native form field's validation message, styled at a small size in the danger foreground color.
field-error.description:
Renders a field's validation message. `id` falls back to `handle.id` so
a sibling `aria-describedby` can target it via `data-field-error`; pass
`hidden` to keep it out of layout until the field is invalid.

file-trigger.name: FileTrigger
file-trigger.definition:
A pressable surface that opens the platform's file picker, backed by a
native `<input type="file">` wrapped in a `<label>` so the platform itself
handles the trigger-to-picker wiring. Its visible content renders inside
the same label as a button-like surface, colored, weighted, and sized
through the same semantic contract as this library's other pressable
controls.
file-trigger.summary: A pressable surface that opens the platform's file picker, backed by a native `<input type="file">` wrapped in a `<label>` so the platform itself handles the trigger-to-picker wiring.
file-trigger.description:
Renders a native `<input type="file">` wrapped in a `<label>` styled
through this library's shared `data-color`/`data-variant`/`data-size`
contract; in dev mode, content lacking an accessible name logs a warning.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: variant
rows.description: Visual weight. Defaults to DEFAULT_VARIANT.

rows.name: size
rows.description: Size variant. Defaults to DEFAULT_SIZE.

rows.name: acceptDirectory
rows.description: Switches the picker from choosing individual files to choosing whole directories, carrying every file nested inside the chosen directory.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The trigger's visible content, rendered inside the same `<label>` that wraps the host `<input>` — an icon, text, or both, kept decorative so the platform's label-to-control association reaches the input on click.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for this component's internally composed elements.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

types.name: Variant
types.description: Visual weight the trigger renders with: a solid fill with an on-solid foreground, a transparent fill with a strong colored border, or a fully transparent fill with just a colored label.

types.name: Size
types.description: Size variant controlling the trigger's padding and font size.

form.name: Form
form.definition:
The wrapper every multi-field layout starts from: a native `<form>` laying
its children out in a single spaced column, and the point where a parsed
validation result enters the tree. Set `issues` from a `parseSafe` (or any
other Standard Schema compliant) result and every field beneath it can
pick out its own errors by name through component context, with no
`issues` prop threaded down by hand.
form.summary: The wrapper every multi-field layout starts from: a native `<form>` laying its children out in a single spaced column, and the point where a parsed validation result enters the tree.
form.description:
Renders a native `<form>` laying children out in a single column, and
provides Form.Context so descendant fields resolve their own
issues by name and focus the first invalid field with no client JS. An
issue with no `path` names no field to attach to, so it renders as its
own leading `Alert` instead of being silently unreachable — a refusal
decided before any field was reached still reaches the person filling
the form in.
examples:
let result = parseSafe(ContactSchema, formData);
<Form method="post" issues={result.success ? undefined : result.issues}>
  <TextField name="email" label={t("contact.email")} />
  <Button type="submit">{t("contact.submit")}</Button>
</Form>

rows.name: issues
rows.description: Validation issues from a `parseSafe` (or equivalent Standard Schema) result, provided to every descendant field through component context. Defaults to no issues, matching a first render.

grid-list.name: GridList
grid-list.definition:
An interactive row list built from plain, already-ordered markup: each
GridList.Item carries a stable key a paired selection,
keyboard-navigation, or reorder behavior can read, while the list itself
renders as a fully static document by default. GridList.Section
groups related rows under an optional GridList.Header label,
GridList.LoadMoreItem holds a trailing loading placeholder, and
GridList.DragHandle marks the one element inside a row a
pointer-driven reorder behavior may grab.
grid-list.summary: An interactive row list built from plain, already-ordered markup: each GridList.Item carries a stable key a paired selection, keyboard-navigation, or reorder behavior can read, while the list itself renders as a fully static document by default.
grid-list.description:
Renders the list's root host as a bordered `<div>` with `role="grid"`,
keeping its row-list layer in an inner wrapper since a `@container` query
can't resolve against the host that declares it; reach `parts.list` to adjust it.
examples:
<GridList aria-label={t("gallery.title")} layout="grid">
	<GridList.Item id="photo-1">{t("gallery.photo", { name: "Sunset" })}</GridList.Item>
	<GridList.Item id="photo-2">{t("gallery.photo", { name: "Harbor" })}</GridList.Item>
</GridList>

rows.name: layout
rows.description: Row arrangement. Defaults to DEFAULT_LAYOUT.

rows.name: children
rows.description: GridList.Item, GridList.Section, and GridList.LoadMoreItem rows to render.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the list's internal row-list wrapper.

parts.name: GridList.Item
parts.description: Renders a single row: a `<div>` carrying `role="row"`, its `id` mirrored onto a `data-rmx-key` attribute so a paired selection, keyboard-navigation, or reorder behavior can correlate the row with its own state.

rows.name: id
rows.description: Stable identifier for this row, mirrored onto both the rendered element's own `id` and a `data-rmx-key` attribute, so the row is already correlation-ready for a paired behavior once one is attached.

parts.name: GridList.Section
parts.description: Renders a titled group of rows: a `<div>` carrying `role="rowgroup"`, stacking an optional GridList.Header above its GridList.Item rows, with a block-start rule before every section but the first.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The section's optional GridList.Header label, followed by its GridList.Item rows.

parts.name: GridList.Header
parts.description: Renders a section's label: a `<header>` styled as small, muted, uppercase text for the GridList.Item rows nested beneath it in a GridList.Section; point the section's `aria-labelledby` at its `id`.

parts.name: GridList.DragHandle
parts.description: Renders the drag-grab element of a row: a native `<button type="button">` written before the consumer's own attributes, so a `command`/`commandfor` pair still runs inside a `<form>` — a `type` seen only after them is ignored.

rows.name: "aria-label"
rows.description: Accessible name for the icon-only control, e.g. "Reorder" or "Drag to reorder".

types.name: Layout
types.description: Arrangement of GridList.Item rows: `"stack"` renders them as a single column, `"grid"` wraps them into a multi-column layout growing from two columns up to four as the list's own container widens.

group.name: Group
group.definition:
A visual and semantic wrapper binding a cluster of related controls into
one unit — a text input paired with its clear button, a row of segmented
buttons, a search field with a trailing submit action. The host lays its
children out in a single row and gains a keyboard focus ring around the
whole cluster whenever a control inside it becomes focus-visible, detected
structurally rather than through any tracked state.
group.summary: A visual and semantic wrapper binding a cluster of related controls into one unit — a text input paired with its clear button, a row of segmented buttons, a search field with a trailing submit action.
group.description:
Lays children out in a centered flex row with no border, background, or
gap, so controls can compose their own edges into one shape, and shows a
keyboard focus ring (primary, or danger under `aria-invalid="true"`).

header.name: Header
header.definition:
A small, muted section label rendered inside a native `<header>` element —
the heading that introduces a group of related items inside a listbox,
menu, or combobox section. It carries no interactive behavior of its own,
only the compact uppercase typography that sets it apart from the items
beneath it.
header.summary: A small, muted section label rendered inside a native `<header>` element — the heading that introduces a group of related items inside a listbox, menu, or combobox section.
header.description:
Renders its children inside a `<header>` element styled as a small,
muted, uppercase section label — the heading introducing a group of
related items inside a listbox, menu, or combobox section.

heading-scope.name: HeadingScope
heading-scope.definition:
Establishes an ambient heading level read by nested headings and scopes,
keeping a document outline sequential without passing a level by hand.
Nesting moves one level deeper unless an explicit `level` fixes it, and
renders a `display: contents` host so composing it adds no layout box
while still exposing the depth via `data-heading-level`.
heading-scope.summary: Establishes an ambient heading level read by nested headings and scopes, keeping a document outline sequential without passing a level by hand.
heading-scope.description:
Establishes an ambient heading level for descendants: an explicit `level`
fixes it, otherwise one level past the nearest ancestor HeadingScope,
read before this scope publishes its own depth, or `1` with no ancestor.

rows.name: level
rows.description: Explicit semantic depth for this scope. Defaults to one level past the nearest ancestor scope's depth, or `1` where no scope wraps this one at all.

heading.name: Heading
heading.definition:
A section title rendered inside the native heading element matching its
semantic depth — `<h1>` through `<h6>` — styled at one fixed emphasis size
regardless of which level it renders. An explicit `level` prop fixes the
depth outright; otherwise, the nearest ancestor `HeadingScope` supplies
it, and a heading with no scope wrapping it at all renders as `<h1>`.
Choosing a level changes only the document outline the element contributes to
assistive technology; its rendered size stays fixed, so nesting sections
correctly never requires a visual trade-off.
heading.summary: A section title rendered inside the native heading element matching its semantic depth — `<h1>` through `<h6>` — styled at one fixed emphasis size regardless of which level it renders.
heading.description:
Renders its children inside the native heading element matching `level`,
styled at one fixed emphasis size — semibold, tight-tracked, and colored for
emphasis, with line height collapsed for compact wrapping.

rows.name: level
rows.description: Semantic depth. Defaults to the nearest ancestor `HeadingScope`'s depth, or `1` where no scope wraps this heading at all.

hover-card.name: HoverCard
hover-card.definition:
A supplementary detail panel that appears beside a trigger on hover or
keyboard focus — a user card beneath an @mention, a definition beneath a
term. Its panel shares Popover's rounded, bordered, shadowed
surface, sized narrower and padded for a compact block of text. Reveal
rides `:hover` and `:focus-within` on the compound root, since a
hover-revealed surface has no invoker to click — the hover path sits
behind `@media (hover: hover)` to avoid a stuck-open panel on coarse
pointers, while focus stays unconditional for keyboard and touch users.
hover-card.summary: A supplementary detail panel that appears beside a trigger on hover or keyboard focus — a user card beneath an @mention, a definition beneath a term.
hover-card.description:
Renders the compound root: a `<span>` providing HoverCard.Content's
anchor and the hover/focus-within scope that reveals it, so hovering or
focusing the trigger or panel keeps it open with no script-tracked state.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The compound root's parts: HoverCard.Trigger followed by HoverCard.Content.

parts.name: HoverCard.Trigger
parts.description: Renders HoverCard.TriggerProps.children inside a `<span>` styled `display: contents`, so the trigger keeps the child's own layout and hover/focus-within participation, visible straight through to the root above.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The visible trigger — a link, button, or other element. The root reveals HoverCard.Content whenever focus or a hover-capable pointer rests inside it, so pointer users reach the panel even without a focusable child.

parts.name: HoverCard.Content
parts.description: Renders the panel: a `<div>` sharing Popover's surface and placement contract, kept in normal stacking order for its CSS-driven hover/focus reveal, with delays tuned for pointer and keyboard users.

rows.name: placement
rows.description: Side of the trigger to render against. Defaults to DEFAULT_PLACEMENT.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The panel's content.

types.name: Placement
types.description: Side of the trigger the panel renders against, and — for corner variants — which trigger edge it aligns to on the perpendicular axis.

image-placeholder.name: ImagePlaceholder
image-placeholder.definition:
The shared foundation for a fixed-size image-with-fallback box — a user
avatar, a brand logo, or any other picture that needs a graceful stand-in
before it loads or when it's missing. It renders a sized, shaped host that
an image and a fallback layer both stack into, plus a corner status badge
and a group of overlapping instances with a trailing overflow count.
image-placeholder.summary: The shared foundation for a fixed-size image-with-fallback box — a user avatar, a brand logo, or any other picture that needs a graceful stand-in before it loads or when it's missing.
image-placeholder.description:
Renders the placeholder host: a fixed-size, centered box whose `data-shape`
attribute styles it, its image, and its fallback together, leaving room
for ImagePlaceholder.Badge to sit unclipped on the corner.

rows.name: size
rows.description: Size variant. Defaults to DEFAULT_SIZE.

rows.name: shape
rows.description: Shape variant. Defaults to DEFAULT_SHAPE.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The host's compound parts: ImagePlaceholder.Image, ImagePlaceholder.Fallback, and an optional ImagePlaceholder.Badge.

parts.name: ImagePlaceholder.Image
parts.description: Renders the placeholder's image layer: an `` cropped with `object-fit: cover`, clipped to ImagePlaceholder's `data-shape`.

rows.name: src
rows.description: Image source URL.

rows.name: alt
rows.description: Accessible text description of the image. Required, since a consumer's own localized description drives what assistive technology announces.

parts.name: ImagePlaceholder.Fallback
parts.description: Renders the placeholder's fallback layer: a `<span>` centering a consumer's content in uppercase text.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Fallback content, typically the subject's initials.

parts.name: ImagePlaceholder.Badge
parts.description: Renders a small status dot pinned to the host's block-end/inline-end corner, always fully rounded regardless of ImagePlaceholder's own shape, and ringed to read as cut from whatever sits beneath it.

parts.name: ImagePlaceholder.Group
parts.description: Renders a row of overlapping placeholders: a flex container that pulls each child back over the previous one and rings each in the neutral tint background, so the overlap reads as stacked cutouts.

rows.name: children
rows.description: A run of ImagePlaceholder instances, optionally trailed by ImagePlaceholder.GroupCount.

parts.name: ImagePlaceholder.GroupCount
parts.description: Renders the "+N" overflow indicator trailing ImagePlaceholder.Group: a fixed medium-size box matching ImagePlaceholder's dimensions and ring treatment, taking its own `shape` prop to match the sibling placeholders.

rows.name: shape
rows.description: Shape variant, matching the shape of the sibling placeholders it trails. Defaults to DEFAULT_SHAPE.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The overflow count text, e.g. `"+3"`.

types.name: Size
types.description: Size variant controlling the host's rendered dimensions and, through ordinary inheritance, the fallback initials' font size.

types.name: Shape
types.description: Shape variant controlling the corner rounding of the host, its image, and its fallback layer: `"circle"` renders a fully rounded disc, and `"square"` renders a softly rounded square.

input.name: Input
input.definition:
A single-line native form field for free text entry, rendered as a
bordered, rounded `<input>` whose border, background, and focus ring read
from a semantic color role. It supplies the field's own box styling only,
ready to compose alongside a paired label, hint, and validation message,
and serves as the shared foundation every other single-line text control
in this library builds on.
input.summary: A single-line native form field for free text entry, rendered as a bordered, rounded `<input>` whose border, background, and focus ring read from a semantic color role.
input.description:
Renders a native `<input>` host colored via `data-color`, with hover,
focus, and disabled states driven by native pseudo-classes; `[aria-invalid="true"]`
together with `:user-invalid` forces the danger tone regardless of `color`.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role for the focus-visible ring, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

item.name: Item
item.definition:
A single-line content row composing a leading media slot, a title and
description content slot, and a trailing action slot along one
horizontally centered line — the shape a settings row, a notification
list entry, or a file row all share. Every part lays out through the
row's own flex line rather than any part reading a semantic role from its
neighbors, so a row renders correctly whichever parts a given list needs:
media and content alone, content and actions alone, or all three.
item.summary: A single-line content row composing a leading media slot, a title and description content slot, and a trailing action slot along one horizontally centered line — the shape a settings row, a notification list entry, or a file row all share.
item.description:
Renders the row's host: a `<div>` laying Item.Media,
Item.Content, and Item.Actions on one flex line, dropping
Item.Actions to a second line once the row narrows past threshold.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's compound parts: Item.Media, Item.Content, and Item.Actions.

parts.name: Item.Media
parts.description: Renders Item.MediaProps.children as the row's leading slot: a shrink-proof, centered `<div>` colored from the neutral foreground so a nested icon inherits it through `currentcolor`.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The leading graphic — an icon, an image thumbnail, an Avatar instance, or a checkbox.

parts.name: Item.Content
parts.description: Renders Item.ContentProps.children as the row's text column: a `<div>` stacking Item.Title and Item.Description with its minimum inline size collapsed to `0` so their truncation takes effect.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Item.Title and, optionally, Item.Description.

parts.name: Item.Title
parts.description: Renders Item.TitleProps.children as the row's label in a plain `<div>`, since a document outline gains nothing from a heading entry per repeated row, truncated to one line in the foreground's emphasized tone.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's label text.

parts.name: Item.Description
parts.description:
Renders Item.DescriptionProps.children as the row's supporting detail in a native `

`, truncated to one line to match Item.Title so the pair reads as one compact two-line block.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Supporting detail below the title — a file size, an email address, a timestamp.

parts.name: Item.Actions
parts.description: Renders Item.ActionsProps.children as the row's trailing slot, pinned to the inline-end edge; once Item wraps narrow, it drops to its own line, indented past Item.Media to read as trailing.

rows.name: children
rows.description: A run of buttons, links, or a switch — whatever control the row offers.

keyboard.name: Keyboard
keyboard.definition:
A keyboard-shortcut hint rendered inside a native `<kbd>` element, sized
and colored as a small muted annotation. Its inline-start auto margin
pushes it to the trailing edge of whatever row it sits in — a menu item's
command, a tooltip's accelerator, a button's shortcut label.
keyboard.summary: A keyboard-shortcut hint rendered inside a native `<kbd>` element, sized and colored as a small muted annotation.
keyboard.description:
Renders its children inside a `<kbd>` element styled as a small, muted
shortcut hint whose inline-start auto margin pushes it to the trailing
edge of whatever row it sits in — a menu item, a tooltip, a button.

label.name: Label
label.definition:
A caption for a form control, associated with its field either through
the native `for`/`id` relationship (set `htmlFor` to the field's `id`) or
by wrapping the control as a child. It renders as a single line of
emphasized text at the library's default label size, weight, and color.
label.summary: A caption for a form control, associated with its field either through the native `for`/`id` relationship (set `htmlFor` to the field's `id`) or by wrapping the control as a child.
label.description:
Renders its children inside a native `<label>` element, sized and colored
as a form field caption. Pair it with a field by setting `htmlFor` to the
field's `id`, or wrap the field directly so the platform associates them.

link-button.name: LinkButton
link-button.definition:
A navigation action styled to read as a button rather than inline text —
"View project", "Download", a dialog's "Cancel" that also navigates away.
Its host renders as a native `<a>`, sharing Button's semantic
color role, visual weight variant, and size so a link and a button placed
side by side render pixel-identical.
link-button.summary: A navigation action styled to read as a button rather than inline text — "View project", "Download", a dialog's "Cancel" that also navigates away.
link-button.description:
Renders a native `<a>` host, colored and shaped through the same color,
variant, and size data attributes as Button. `aria-disabled="true"`
keeps it focusable while dimmed, so drop `href` too for full inertness.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

types.name: Variant
types.description: Visual weight the link renders with: a solid fill with an on-solid foreground, a transparent fill with a strong colored border, or a fully transparent fill with just a colored label.

types.name: Size
types.description: Size variant controlling the link's padding and font size.

link.name: Link
link.definition:
A native anchor for inline navigation, always underlined so its
affordance never rests on color alone, and colored through a semantic
color role that also drives its focus ring and disabled state.
link.summary: A native anchor for inline navigation, always underlined so its affordance never rests on color alone, and colored through a semantic color role that also drives its focus ring and disabled state.
link.description:
Renders a native `<a>` host, colored through the `data-color` attribute
contract and underlined unconditionally. `aria-disabled="true"` mutes the
link, but only removing or neutralizing `href` actually stops navigation.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

listbox.name: ListBox
listbox.definition:
A run of selectable option rows sharing one native grouping name — each
ListBox.Item pairs a visually hidden `<input type="radio">` or
`<input type="checkbox">` with its own visible content, so every focus,
keyboard, and form-submission semantic keeps coming from the platform
itself. The host renders as a scrollable column reading each option's
`:checked` and `:focus` state through a `:has()` selector to color the
whole row, with no selection state tracked anywhere in this module.
listbox.summary: A run of selectable option rows sharing one native grouping name — each ListBox.Item pairs a visually hidden `<input type="radio">` or `<input type="checkbox">` with its own visible content, so every focus, keyboard, and form-submission semantic keeps coming from the platform itself.
listbox.description:
Renders the group host: a `<div>` laying its ListBox.Item options
out as a scrollable column capped at a fixed block size, with `role`
defaulting to `"radiogroup"` for single selection or `"group"` for `multiple`.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native grouping name shared by every ListBox.Item nested inside, provided through component context. Defaults to the group's own stable instance id, so options always group correctly.

rows.name: multiple
rows.description: Renders every option as a checkbox, allowing more than one selected at once, instead of the default mutually exclusive radio behavior. Defaults to DEFAULT_MULTIPLE.

parts.name: ListBox.Item
parts.description: Renders a single option: a native `<label>` pairing a visually hidden radio or checkbox input with the option's content.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Value submitted with the enclosing form when this option is selected.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native grouping name for this option's underlying input. Defaults to the name provided by the nearest ancestor ListBox — set this only to opt a single option out of its group's shared name.

rows.name: defaultChecked
rows.description: Whether this option starts selected, for a form that never tracks selection itself.

rows.name: checked
rows.description: Whether this option is selected, for a form that tracks selection itself.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Whether this option is inert and excluded from the group's tab order.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Sets the underlying input's native `required` attribute. On a radio input this requires at least one option in the group be selected; on a checkbox input it requires this specific option be checked.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The option's visible content, associated with the input by native nesting.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the option's hidden `input` element, layered after its own built-in styling. Use the `mix` prop instead to style the option's outer `<label>` host.

logo.name: Logo
logo.definition:
A brand mark rendered as a fixed-size, softly rounded host stacking an
image layer, an initials fallback, and an optional corner status badge,
plus a way to overlap several instances into one group with a trailing
overflow count.
logo.summary: A brand mark rendered as a fixed-size, softly rounded host stacking an image layer, an initials fallback, and an optional corner status badge, plus a way to overlap several instances into one group with a trailing overflow count.
logo.description:
Renders a fixed-size, softly rounded brand-mark host that stacks whichever
of Logo.Image, Logo.Fallback, and Logo.Badge a
consumer composes as children, with square corner rounding fixed in place.

marker.name: Marker
marker.definition:
An inline row calling out a small event between two message rows — a
delivery status, a system note, a highlighted callout, or a labeled
divider — colored by a semantic tone and shaped by a variant.
Marker.Icon and Marker.Content compose beneath it for a
glyph-plus-caption row.
marker.summary: An inline row calling out a small event between two message rows — a delivery status, a system note, a highlighted callout, or a labeled divider — colored by a semantic tone and shaped by a variant.
marker.description:
Renders the row's host element: a centered flex line framed through the
`data-variant` and `data-color` attributes, with `variant="separator"`
also picking up `role="separator"`.

rows.name: variant
rows.description: Visual shape of the row. Defaults to DEFAULT_VARIANT.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's compound parts: Marker.Icon followed by Marker.Content.

parts.name: Marker.Icon
parts.description: Renders Marker.IconProps.children as the row's glyph slot, hidden from assistive technology unless a consumer overrides it for a nested accessible control like Spinner.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The icon graphic, typically a single SVG icon, or a nested control such as Spinner.

parts.name: Marker.Content
parts.description: Renders Marker.ContentProps.children as the row's caption: a `<span>` inheriting its color, size, and weight from the Marker root so a single `data-color` drives the icon and caption together.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's caption text.

types.name: Variant
types.description: Visual shape the row renders with: `"default"` for a plain, centered caption, `"border"` for a bordered, tinted callout panel, and `"separator"` for a caption flanked by a hairline divider on either side.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

menu.name: Menu
menu.definition:
A menu surface anchored to whatever invoker opens it, riding the same
native Popover API Popover does, sized to its own content and
padded around a compact stack of Menu.Item rows, Menu.Separator dividers, or a `Section`/`Header` pair grouping related
rows together. Every row lands in the page's native Tab order out of the
box, since each renders as a real `<a>` or `<button>`.
menu.summary: A menu surface anchored to whatever invoker opens it, riding the same native Popover API Popover does, sized to its own content and padded around a compact stack of Menu.Item rows, Menu.Separator dividers, or a `Section`/`Header` pair grouping related rows together.
menu.description:
Renders the menu's own host: a Popover defaulting to
`"bottom-start"` placement and `"menu"` role, sized to its content. Point a
row's `commandfor` at another `<Menu>`'s `id` to open it as a nested menu.
examples:
<Menu id="row-menu" placement="left-start" aria-label={t("table.rowActions")}>
	<Section aria-labelledby="row-menu-view-heading">
		<Header id="row-menu-view-heading">{t("menu.view")}</Header>
		<Menu.Item href={viewUrl}>{t("actions.view")}</Menu.Item>
		<Menu.Item href={editUrl}>{t("actions.edit")}</Menu.Item>
	</Section>
	<Menu.Separator />
	<Menu.Item danger commandfor="confirm-delete" command="show-modal">{t("actions.delete")}</Menu.Item>
</Menu>

rows.name: children
rows.description: The menu's rows: Menu.Item, Menu.Separator, or a `Section`/`Header` pair grouping related items together.

parts.name: Menu.Item
parts.description: Renders a native `<a>` when `href` is set, else a `<button>`, defaulting `role` to `"menuitem"`; only omitting or neutralizing `href` stops the `<a>` variant's navigation, since `aria-disabled` mutes it visually only.

rows.name: href
rows.description: Destination the row navigates to. Renders the row as a native `<a>` instead of a `<button>` when set.

rows.name: target
rows.description: `target` for the link variant, applied only once `href` is set.

rows.name: rel
rows.description: `rel` for the link variant, applied only once `href` is set.

rows.name: danger
rows.description: Styles the row in the semantic danger tone, for a destructive action like deleting a resource.

rows.name: mix
rows.description: Extra mixin(s) applied to the row's host element, whichever of `<a>`/`<button>` it renders as depending on href.

parts.name: Menu.Separator
parts.description: Renders a hairline divider between two runs of Menu.Items: the shared Separator component with the small block-axis margin a menu's compact rows need on either side of it.

menubar.name: Menubar
menubar.definition:
A horizontal row of top-level triggers modeled on a native application's
menu bar, where each trigger opens its own dropdown built from the
existing Menu component.
menubar.summary: A horizontal row of top-level triggers modeled on a native application's menu bar, where each trigger opens its own dropdown built from the existing Menu component.
menubar.description:
Renders the row's host: a native `<div>` carrying the `menubar` role for
Menubar.Triggers. In dev mode, a root missing an `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby` logs a `console.warn`.

parts.name: Menubar.Trigger
parts.description: Renders a single top-level trigger: a native `<button>` pointed at the `id` of the Menu it opens through `commandfor`, with `command` defaulting to `"toggle-popover"` and `role` to `"menuitem"`.

rows.name: commandfor
rows.description: `id` of the Menu this trigger opens.

message-scroller.name: MessageScroller
message-scroller.definition:
A scrollable frame for a conversational message log. Its viewport reuses
the same scrollbar treatment every scrolling surface in this catalog
shares and fades its own edges to hint at history above and replies still
below; its content region announces newly appended rows through the ARIA
log role; each row carries the message id and anchor data a scroll-follow
behavior reads; and a static jump-to-latest control sits ready for that
same behavior to reveal.
message-scroller.summary: A scrollable frame for a conversational message log.
message-scroller.description:
Renders the frame's root host: a bordered, rounded `<div>` that
declares the `ui-message-scroller` container queried by
MessageScroller.Button for its own placement.
examples:
<MessageScroller mix={css({ blockSize: "32rem" })}>
	<MessageScroller.Viewport>
		<MessageScroller.Content aria-busy={isStreaming}>
			<MessageScroller.Item messageId={turn.id} scrollAnchor>
				{turn.content}
			</MessageScroller.Item>
		</MessageScroller.Content>
	</MessageScroller.Viewport>
	<MessageScroller.Button aria-label={t("chat.jumpToLatest")} />
</MessageScroller>

rows.name: children
rows.description: The frame's compound parts: MessageScroller.Viewport and, optionally, MessageScroller.Button.

parts.name: MessageScroller.Viewport
parts.description: Renders the frame's scrolling surface as ScrollArea.Viewport, fixed to the block axis.

rows.name: children
rows.description: MessageScroller.Content, scrolling inside the viewport.

parts.name: MessageScroller.Content
parts.description: Renders the frame's live region: a `<div>` carrying the ARIA log role, stacking its MessageScroller.Item rows in a column and announcing each added row via `aria-relevant="additions"`.

rows.name: "aria-busy"
rows.description: Marks the log as busy while a row inside it is still being written to — a reply still streaming in, for instance — forwarded to the host's native `aria-busy` attribute. Clear it once the row settles.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The MessageScroller.Item rows to render in document order.

parts.name: MessageScroller.Item
parts.description: Renders a single message row: a `<div>` mirroring `messageId` onto `data-message-id` and, when `scrollAnchor` is set, an empty `data-scroll-anchor` attribute for a scroll-follow behavior to read.

rows.name: messageId
rows.description: Stable id of the message this row renders, mirrored onto the host's `data-message-id` attribute so a scroll-follow behavior can find, measure, and scroll to this exact row directly.

rows.name: scrollAnchor
rows.description: Marks this row as a candidate anchor point — typically the first row of a new turn — mirrored onto `data-scroll-anchor` so a scroll-follow behavior can tell which rows are worth anchoring the viewport to.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's own content, typically a conversational row composed inside it.

parts.name: MessageScroller.Button
parts.description: Renders a static jump-to-latest control as Button, floating over the frame's block-end edge and starting `hidden` until a paired scroll-follow behavior clears the attribute.

rows.name: hidden
rows.description: Whether the control is absent from rendering and the accessibility tree. A paired scroll-follow behavior clears this attribute as the reader scrolls away from the live edge and sets it again on return or press.

message.name: Message
message.definition:
A single conversational turn in a message log: a row composing a
bottom-anchored avatar, a header for the sender's identity and timing, a
content slot for the message's own surface, and an optional footer for its
actions. Compound parts lay out entirely through CSS grid areas keyed off
each part's `data-slot`, so the avatar's vertical anchor and the footer's
presence never need to be tracked as state.
message.summary: A single conversational turn in a message log: a row composing a bottom-anchored avatar, a header for the sender's identity and timing, a content slot for the message's own surface, and an optional footer for its actions.
message.description:
Renders the message row as a two-column grid whose `"avatar"` area spans only the
header and content rows, anchoring Message.Avatar to the bottom edge
of Message.Content, regardless of whether Message.Footer renders.
examples: {sender.initials} {sender.name} {formattedTime} {message.text}

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's compound parts: Message.Avatar, Message.Header, Message.Content, and an optional Message.Footer.

parts.name: Message.Avatar
parts.description: Renders Message.AvatarProps.children as the row's avatar slot, aligned to the `"avatar"` area's block-end edge so it tracks the bottom edge of Message.Content.

rows.name: children
rows.description: An Avatar instance identifying the message's sender.

parts.name: Message.Header
parts.description: Renders Message.HeaderProps.children as the row's identity line, wrapping until the `ui-message` container passes `26rem`, then settling onto one row with the sender's name first and later children as secondary metadata.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The sender's name, typically followed by a timestamp.

parts.name: Message.Content
parts.description: Renders Message.ContentProps.children as the row's content slot, capped to a comfortable reading measure and never narrower than its grid area.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The message's own surface — a Bubble, an attachment card, or any other rendered turn content.

parts.name: Message.Footer
parts.description: Renders Message.FooterProps.children as the row's action slot, occupying the grid's `"footer"` area beneath Message.Content and never reached by Message.Avatar's bottom anchor.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The row's actions, typically a copy Button and a like Button.

parts.name: Message.Group
parts.description: Renders Message.GroupProps.children as a run of consecutive Message rows sharing the same sender, stacked with a hairline gap that reads as one continuous turn.

rows.name: children
rows.description: A run of consecutive Message rows sharing the same sender.

meter.name: Meter
meter.definition:
A styled native `<meter>` gauge paired with an optional value label,
stacked in a single column so a caption can sit alongside the bar it
measures. The gauge's track and fill read entirely from the control's own
`value`/`min`/`max` attributes, tinted by a semantic color role chosen
independently of the platform's own optimum/suboptimum quality coloring.
meter.summary: A styled native `<meter>` gauge paired with an optional value label, stacked in a single column so a caption can sit alongside the bar it measures.
meter.description:
Renders the root column: a `<div>` stacking Meter.Indicator and an
optional Meter.ValueLabel with a small gap. The native `<meter>`
inside already exposes the platform's meter semantics.

parts.name: Meter.Indicator
parts.description: Renders the gauge as a pill-shaped track filled in a semantic `color`, mirrored across each engine's fill pseudo-elements so `low`/`high`/`optimum` keep shaping accessible semantics independently of the rendered color; dev mode warns when no accessible name is set.

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the gauge's fill. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

parts.name: Meter.ValueLabel
parts.description: Renders the gauge's caption: a `<span>` sized as a small run of body copy in the neutral muted foreground color, for a percentage or status string placed alongside Meter.Indicator.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*-bg-solid` variable for the gauge's filled portion.

modal.name: Modal
modal.definition:
A pre-animated preset of Dialog: the same native `<dialog>` panel,
its `::backdrop` treatment, and every compound part, with the panel's own
pop-in and pop-out motion — a fade paired with a scale, entering from
slightly smaller and less opaque than rest and exiting back down to it —
already wired onto the host.
modal.summary: A pre-animated preset of Dialog: the same native `<dialog>` panel, its `::backdrop` treatment, and every compound part, with the panel's own pop-in and pop-out motion — a fade paired with a scale, entering from slightly smaller and less opaque than rest and exiting back down to it — already wired onto the host.
modal.description:
Renders Dialog with its panel's pop-in/pop-out motion pre-wired
through `mix`, collapsing to an opacity-only fade under reduced motion.
A `mix` passed to Modal layers alongside the built-in motion.
examples:
<Modal id="confirm-delete" aria-labelledby="confirm-delete-title">
	<Modal.Close commandfor="confirm-delete" aria-label={t("actions.close")} />
	<Modal.Header>
		<Modal.Title id="confirm-delete-title">{t("project.deleteTitle")}</Modal.Title>
		<Modal.Description>{t("project.deleteDescription")}</Modal.Description>
	</Modal.Header>
	<Modal.Footer>
		<Button commandfor="confirm-delete" command="close" color="danger">{t("actions.delete")}</Button>
	</Modal.Footer>
</Modal>

nav-link.name: NavLink
nav-link.definition:
An inline text link for site navigation, colored through a semantic color
role and underlined to read as a link among surrounding prose. Its
current-page state comes straight from `aria-current` set on the host
server-side, rendering the emphasized, non-underlined treatment directly
from that attribute.
nav-link.summary: An inline text link for site navigation, colored through a semantic color role and underlined to read as a link among surrounding prose.
nav-link.description:
Renders a native `<a>`, colored via `data-color` and underlined with a
translucent decoration that solidifies on hover. Setting `aria-current`
server-side renders the current-page treatment; the focus-visible ring always reads in the primary color.

types.name: Color
types.description: Semantic color role, each mapped to its matching `--ui-*` variables.

navigation-menu.name: NavigationMenu
navigation-menu.definition:
A row of top-level navigation triggers, each either a plain link or a
button that opens a floating panel of related links. `NavigationMenu.Item`
hands its own stable id to whichever `NavigationMenu.Trigger` and
`NavigationMenu.Content` nest inside it through component context, so the
two pair up automatically — a consumer never wires a `commandfor`/`id`
pair by hand for the common case.
navigation-menu.summary: A row of top-level navigation triggers, each either a plain link or a button that opens a floating panel of related links.
navigation-menu.description:
Renders the menu's root host: a native `<nav>` landmark establishing a
positioning context for whatever floating panels its
NavigationMenu.Content instances anchor against.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The menu's own NavigationMenu.List, and anything else rendered alongside it (a NavigationMenu.Viewport, for instance).

parts.name: NavigationMenu.List
parts.description: Renders the row of top-level triggers: a native `<ul>` laying its NavigationMenu.Items out horizontally by default, switching to a single start-aligned column when `orientation` is `"vertical"`.

rows.name: orientation
rows.description: Layout axis. Defaults to DEFAULT_ORIENTATION.

rows.name: children
rows.description: One or more NavigationMenu.Items.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.Item
parts.description: Renders a single top-level entry: a native `<li>` holding either a standalone NavigationMenu.Link or a NavigationMenu.Trigger paired with the NavigationMenu.Content it opens.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Either a standalone NavigationMenu.Link, or a NavigationMenu.Trigger followed by the NavigationMenu.Content it opens.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.Trigger
parts.description: Renders a native `<button>` that opens the enclosing NavigationMenu.Item's NavigationMenu.Content through the Invoker Commands API, so `aria-expanded` reflects the panel automatically.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.Content
parts.description: Renders NavigationMenu.Content, the floating panel a NavigationMenu.Trigger opens: a Popover that fades and scales itself using the platform's own `:popover-open` state.

rows.name: id
rows.description: Stable id matched against a NavigationMenu.Trigger's `commandfor`. Defaults to the enclosing NavigationMenu.Item's generated id.

rows.name: placement
rows.description: Side of the trigger to render against. Defaults to DEFAULT_CONTENT_PLACEMENT.

rows.name: size
rows.description: Panel width. Defaults to DEFAULT_CONTENT_SIZE.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.Link
parts.description: Renders NavigationMenu.LinkProps.children as a native `<a>`.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.Viewport
parts.description: Renders a shared, animated surface that swaps in the active NavigationMenu.Item's content, sized by the custom properties a pairing mixin writes as it measures the active panel and toggles visibility.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The currently active item's content, mirrored in from wherever it actually renders.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.ContentList
parts.description: Renders NavigationMenu.ContentListProps.children as a plain vertical run of NavigationMenu.Links inside NavigationMenu.Content, for a dropdown that's just a short list.

rows.name: children
rows.description: One or more NavigationMenu.Links.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.ContentGrid
parts.description: Renders NavigationMenu.ContentGridProps.children as a multi-column layout inside NavigationMenu.Content: a single column while the panel's own container is narrower than `40rem`, else two columns.

rows.name: children
rows.description: Two or more NavigationMenu.ContentColumns.

parts.name: NavigationMenu.ContentColumn
parts.description: Renders NavigationMenu.ContentColumnProps.children as one column of stacked NavigationMenu.Links inside a NavigationMenu.ContentGrid.

rows.name: children
rows.description: One or more NavigationMenu.Links.

types.name: Orientation
types.description: Axis NavigationMenu.List lays its triggers out along: a single row, or a single column.

types.name: ContentSize
types.description: Panel width NavigationMenu.Content renders at: sized to its own content (`"default"`), or a fixed, generously wide measure that still clamps to the viewport on narrow screens (`"wide"`).

number-field.name: NumberField
number-field.definition:
A numeric field pairing a native `<input type="number">` control with a
decrement and an increment button, all three sharing one bordered,
rounded frame. The frame draws its own box styling and keyboard focus
ring, so the input inside sits flush against its neighboring buttons
instead of carrying a competing border of its own.
number-field.summary: A numeric field pairing a native `<input type="number">` control with a decrement and an increment button, all three sharing one bordered, rounded frame.
number-field.description:
Renders a plain host stacking this field's compound parts in a single
column with a small gap between them: typically a caption, the
NumberField.Group row, and any supporting or validation copy.
examples:
<NumberField>
	<Label htmlFor="quantity">{t("form.quantity.label")}</Label>
	<NumberField.Group>
		<NumberField.DecrementButton aria-label={t("stepper.decrement")} />
		<NumberField.Input id="quantity" name="quantity" min={0} max={10} defaultValue={1} />
		<NumberField.IncrementButton aria-label={t("stepper.increment")} />
	</NumberField.Group>
</NumberField>

parts.name: NumberField.Group
parts.description: Renders NumberField's frame: a `role="group"` `<div>` drawing a bordered, rounded, tinted-background box that reads as one seamless control, ringing the whole frame via `:focus-within` when a child gains focus.

parts.name: NumberField.Input
parts.description: Renders NumberField's control: a native `<input type="number">` built on Input.

parts.name: NumberField.DecrementButton
parts.description: Renders a native `<button>` decrementing NumberField.Input's value; its glyph is `aria-hidden`, so callers must supply an `aria-label`.

parts.name: NumberField.IncrementButton
parts.description: Renders a native `<button>` incrementing NumberField.Input's value; its glyph is `aria-hidden`, so callers must supply an `aria-label`.

otp-field.name: OtpField
otp-field.definition:
A one-time-code field: a native `<input>` defaulting to a numeric virtual
keyboard and the platform's SMS/email autofill hint for one-time codes,
built on Input for its box, color, and interaction-state styling.
otp-field.summary: A one-time-code field: a native `<input>` defaulting to a numeric virtual keyboard and the platform's SMS/email autofill hint for one-time codes, built on Input for its box, color, and interaction-state styling.
otp-field.description:
Renders a single native `<input>` for entering a one-time verification
code, built on Input, sized as one full-width control since a
single `<input>` is what carries `autoComplete="one-time-code"` reliably.
examples:
<OtpField
	id="invite-code"
	name="inviteCode"
	length={8}
	inputMode="text"
	autoComplete="off"
	pattern="[A-Za-z0-9]*"
/>

rows.name: length
rows.description: The one-time code's character count, applied as the control's native `maxLength`. Defaults to DEFAULT_LENGTH.

rows.name: inputMode
rows.description: Virtual-keyboard hint passed straight through to the native `inputMode` attribute. Defaults to DEFAULT_INPUT_MODE, requesting the numeric keypad; set it to `"text"` for a code that mixes in letters.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Platform autofill hint passed straight through to the native `autoComplete` attribute. Defaults to DEFAULT_AUTO_COMPLETE, which a browser or OS keyboard looks for to offer an SMS or email code inline.

overlay-arrow.name: OverlayArrow
overlay-arrow.definition:
A small pointer glyph anchoring an overlay surface — a popover, a menu, a
tooltip — visually back to the trigger it floats beside. It renders as an
absolutely positioned host holding whatever arrow shape a consumer draws
as its child (typically an inline `<svg>`), oriented and offset by the
`data-placement` attribute contract.
overlay-arrow.summary: A small pointer glyph anchoring an overlay surface — a popover, a menu, a tooltip — visually back to the trigger it floats beside.
overlay-arrow.description:
Renders a decorative pointer glyph, rotating to point back at the trigger
from whichever edge the overlay attaches to. `"left"`/`"right"` name a
physical viewport side, so the arrow keeps attaching there under any `dir`.
examples:
<Popover>
	<OverlayArrow placement="bottom">
		<svg width={12} height={12} viewBox="0 0 12 12">
			<path d="M0 0 L6 6 L12 0" />
		</svg>
	</OverlayArrow>
	{content}
</Popover>

rows.name: placement
rows.description: Side of the trigger the overlay renders on. Defaults to DEFAULT_PLACEMENT.

types.name: Placement
types.description: Side (and, for the four corner variants, alignment) of the trigger an overlay renders relative to.

pagination.name: Pagination
pagination.definition:
A navigation landmark for moving between pages of results, composing a
`<nav>` root, an `<ul>` list, and `<li>` items around two interactive
parts: Pagination.Link for page-number destinations and
Pagination.Button for previous/next controls. The active page reads
straight from the native `aria-current` attribute a consumer sets while
rendering the current page's link server-side, with no client-tracked
route state anywhere in this module.
pagination.summary: A navigation landmark for moving between pages of results, composing a `<nav>` root, an `<ul>` list, and `<li>` items around two interactive parts: Pagination.Link for page-number destinations and Pagination.Button for previous/next controls.
pagination.description:
Renders the pagination's `<nav>` root, laying its single Pagination.List child out as a centered row. In dev mode, a root missing
`aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` logs a `console.warn` for assistive tech.

parts.name: Pagination.List
parts.description: Renders the pagination's `<ul>` list, resetting native list markers and spacing and laying Pagination.Item children out as a centered row with a small gap between them.

parts.name: Pagination.Item
parts.description: Renders a single `<li>` wrapping one Pagination.Link or Pagination.Button, centering its content — this element carries no visual styling of its own beyond the layout needed to hold its child.

parts.name: Pagination.Link
parts.description: Renders a page-number destination as a native `<a>`.

parts.name: Pagination.Button
parts.description: Renders a previous/next control as a native `<button>`.

popover.name: Popover
popover.definition:
A floating surface anchored to whatever element opened it, built entirely
on the native Popover API: the host carries the `popover` attribute and
opens through `popovertarget` or a Command Invoker (`commandfor`/
`command="toggle-popover"`) elsewhere on the page, with no positioning
logic running in script. Placement rides CSS anchor positioning, using
the invoker relationship as an implicit anchor and the `data-placement`
attribute to pick which `position-area` it resolves against.
popover.summary: A floating surface anchored to whatever element opened it, built entirely on the native Popover API: the host carries the `popover` attribute and opens through `popovertarget` or a Command Invoker (`commandfor`/ `command="toggle-popover"`) elsewhere on the page, with no positioning logic running in script.
popover.description:
Renders the floating surface itself: a `popover`-attributed `<div>`
positioned via CSS anchor positioning. The invoker that opens it becomes
the implicit anchor its `position-area` resolves against.
examples:
<Popover id="filters" placement="top" mix={[fade({ duration: durations.normal })]}>
	<OverlayArrow placement="top">
		<svg width={12} height={12} viewBox="0 0 12 12">
			<path d="M0 0 L6 6 L12 0" />
		</svg>
	</OverlayArrow>
	{content}
</Popover>

rows.name: id
rows.description: Stable id an invoker elsewhere on the page targets to open this host.

rows.name: popover
rows.description: `popover` attribute mode: `"auto"` dismisses on outside click or Escape and closes sibling `"auto"` popovers when shown; `"hint"` layers over an open one without closing it; `"manual"` closes only when hidden explicitly.

rows.name: placement
rows.description: Side of the anchor to render against. Defaults to DEFAULT_PLACEMENT.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The popover's content.

types.name: Placement
types.description: Side of the anchor the host renders against, and, for the four corner variants, which anchor edge it aligns to along the perpendicular axis.

progress-bar.name: ProgressBar
progress-bar.definition:
A styled native `<progress>` control paired with an optional value label,
stacked in a single column so a caption can sit alongside the bar it
describes. The indicator's track and fill read entirely from the control's
own `value`/`max` attributes and its native `:indeterminate` state, so a
value-less indicator already renders as busy with zero library JavaScript.
progress-bar.summary: A styled native `<progress>` control paired with an optional value label, stacked in a single column so a caption can sit alongside the bar it describes.
progress-bar.description:
Renders the root column: a `<div>` stacking ProgressBar.Indicator
and an optional ProgressBar.ValueLabel, carrying no ARIA of its
own since the `<progress>` inside already exposes progressbar semantics.

parts.name: ProgressBar.Indicator
parts.description: Renders the busy/progress indicator: a native `<progress>` restyled as a pill track.

parts.name: ProgressBar.ValueLabel
parts.description: Renders the indicator's caption: a `<span>` sized as a small run of body copy in the neutral muted foreground color, for a percentage or status string placed alongside ProgressBar.Indicator.

radio-group.name: RadioGroup
radio-group.definition:
A set of mutually exclusive options built from native `<input
type="radio">` controls sharing one grouping name, rendered as a
`role="radiogroup"` host wrapping a run of RadioGroup.Radio
instances. Each option pairs a visually hidden native input — carrying
every focus, keyboard, and form-submission semantic the platform already
provides — with a styled visual indicator that reads the input's own
`:checked` and `:focus-visible` states through sibling selectors.
radio-group.summary: A set of mutually exclusive options built from native `<input type="radio">` controls sharing one grouping name, rendered as a `role="radiogroup"` host wrapping a run of RadioGroup.Radio instances.
radio-group.description:
Renders the group host: a `role="radiogroup"` `<div>` laying its
RadioGroup.Radio options in a column, or a row when
`orientation` is `"horizontal"`, giving every option a shared, stable `name`.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native grouping name shared by every RadioGroup.Radio nested inside. Defaults to the group's own stable instance id so options group correctly without a consumer setting one.

rows.name: orientation
rows.description: Layout axis. Defaults to DEFAULT_ORIENTATION.

parts.name: RadioGroup.Radio
parts.description: Renders a single option: a `<label>` pairing a hidden native `<input type="radio">` with a styled indicator driven by its checked, focus, and disabled state; add `ariaChecked()` via `parts.input` for `aria-checked`.

rows.name: value
rows.description: Value submitted with the enclosing form when this option is selected.

rows.name: name
rows.description: Native grouping name for this option's underlying input. Defaults to the name provided by the nearest ancestor RadioGroup — set this only to opt a single option out of its group's shared name.

rows.name: defaultChecked
rows.description: Whether this option starts selected, for a form that leaves selection tracking to the browser.

rows.name: checked
rows.description: Whether this option is selected, for a form that tracks selection itself.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Whether this option is inert and excluded from the group's tab order.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks the enclosing native radio group as requiring one option selected.

rows.name: children
rows.description: The option's visible label text, associated with the input by native nesting.

rows.name: parts
rows.description: Per-part styling for the option's hidden `input` and visible `indicator` elements, layered after each part's own built-in styling. Use the `mix` prop instead to style the option's outer `<label>` host.

types.name: Orientation
types.description: Axis a group's options lay out along: a single column, or a single row.

range-calendar.name: RangeCalendar
range-calendar.definition:
A calendar surface for choosing a start and end date as one connected
range, sharing every header, grid, and row part with Calendar and
layering range position on top of its day cell. Used bare, with no
composed children, it renders a pair of native `<input type="date">`
fields instead — start and end, each independently keyboard-operable —
ready for the `calendarKeys()`/`rangePreview()` mixins a consumer attaches
to turn the composed grid into a live, drag- or arrow-key-extended range.
range-calendar.summary: A calendar surface for choosing a start and end date as one connected range, sharing every header, grid, and row part with Calendar and layering range position on top of its day cell.
range-calendar.description:
Renders RangeCalendar's root through Calendar. Composing
RangeCalendar.Header and RangeCalendar.Grid as `children`
renders the visual month surface; omitting `children` renders a bare, script-free native `<input type="date">` pair from this instance's own fields.
examples:
<RangeCalendar aria-label={t("calendar.label")}>
	<RangeCalendar.Header>
		<RangeCalendar.PreviousButton aria-label={t("calendar.previous")} />
		<RangeCalendar.Heading>{monthLabel}</RangeCalendar.Heading>
		<RangeCalendar.NextButton aria-label={t("calendar.next")} />
	</RangeCalendar.Header>
	<RangeCalendar.Grid aria-label={monthLabel}>
		<RangeCalendar.GridHeader>
			<RangeCalendar.Row>
				{weekdayLabels.map((day) => (
					<RangeCalendar.HeaderCell key={day}>{day}</RangeCalendar.HeaderCell>
				))}
			</RangeCalendar.Row>
		</RangeCalendar.GridHeader>
		<RangeCalendar.GridBody>
			{weeks.map((week) => (
				<RangeCalendar.Row key={week[0].iso}>
					{week.map((day) => (
						<RangeCalendar.Cell
							key={day.iso}
							aria-selected={day.inRange ? "true" : undefined}
							data-selection-start={day.iso === range.start ? "" : undefined}
							data-selection-end={day.iso === range.end ? "" : undefined}
						>
							{day.label}
						</RangeCalendar.Cell>
					))}
				</RangeCalendar.Row>
			))}
		</RangeCalendar.GridBody>
	</RangeCalendar.Grid>
</RangeCalendar>

rows.name: color
rows.description: Semantic color role for the bare fallback pair's focus rings. Defaults to DEFAULT_COLOR.

rows.name: startName
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form, read only by the bare fallback's start-date input.

rows.name: endName
rows.description: Native `name` submitted with an enclosing form, read only by the bare fallback's end-date input.

rows.name: startValue
rows.description: Current start-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a bare fallback pair a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: endValue
rows.description: Current end-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a bare fallback pair a consumer tracks itself.

rows.name: startDefaultValue
rows.description: Initial start-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a bare fallback pair left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: endDefaultValue
rows.description: Initial end-of-range value, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, for a bare fallback pair left to the platform's own uncontrolled state.

rows.name: min
rows.description: Earliest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read by both of the bare fallback pair's inputs.

rows.name: max
rows.description: Latest accepted date, in `YYYY-MM-DD` form, read by both of the bare fallback pair's inputs.

rows.name: step
rows.description: Granularity, in days, both of the bare fallback pair's values must fall on.

rows.name: required
rows.description: Marks both of the bare fallback pair's inputs required for their enclosing form.

rows.name: disabled
rows.description: Marks both of the bare fallback pair's inputs inert and excluded from the tab order.

rows.name: readOnly
rows.description: Marks both of the bare fallback pair's inputs' values fixed, while keeping them focusable and included in form submission.

rows.name: autoComplete
rows.description: Native autofill hint for both of the bare fallback pair's inputs, e.g. `"bday"`.

rows.name: startLabel
rows.description: Accessible label for the bare fallback pair's start-date input. Read only when `children` is unset.

rows.name: endLabel
